sentences.zh: 張芹，字文林，峽江人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qin, style name Wenlin, was a native of Xiajiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qin, whose style name was Wenlin, came from Xiajiang.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign (1502).

sentences.zh: 授福州推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 正德中，召為南京御史。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he was summoned to serve as censor at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was summoned to serve as a censor at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 寧夏既平，大學士李東陽亦進官蔭子。

translations.literal: After Ningxia had been pacified, Grand Secretary Li Dongyang also received advancement and ennoblement of his son.
translations.idiomatic: After Ningxia had been pacified, Grand Secretary Li Dongyang was also promoted and granted hereditary privilege for his son.

sentences.zh: 芹抗疏曰：「東陽謹厚有余，正直不足；

translations.literal: Qin submitted a forceful memorial saying: "Dongyang has more than enough prudence and steadiness, but not enough uprightness;
translations.idiomatic: Qin submitted a forceful memorial, saying: "Dongyang is more than sufficiently prudent and steady, yet insufficiently upright;

sentences.zh: 儒雅足重，節義無聞。

translations.literal: his scholarly elegance is weighty enough, but nothing is heard of his integrity and moral resolve.
translations.idiomatic: his scholarly elegance carries weight, but one hears nothing of his integrity or moral resolve.

sentences.zh: 逆瑾亂政，東陽為顧命大臣，既不能遏之於始，及惡跡既彰，又不能力與之抗。

translations.literal: When the rebellious Jin threw the government into disorder, Dongyang was a entrusted minister; he could neither check him at the outset, nor when the evil deeds had become manifest could he exert himself to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the unruly Liu Jin threw the government into disorder, Dongyang was an entrusted minister; he could neither check him at the outset, and once Jin's wicked deeds were plain, he still could not muster the strength to resist him.

sentences.zh: 脂韋順從，惟其指使。

translations.literal: He greased and went along compliantly, doing only as Jin directed.
translations.idiomatic: He flattered and submitted, doing only as Jin directed.

sentences.zh: 今叛賊底平，東陽何力？

translations.literal: Now that the rebel bandits have been settled, what strength did Dongyang exert?
translations.idiomatic: Now that the rebels have been put down, what had Dongyang to do with it?

sentences.zh: 冒功受賞，何以服人心？

translations.literal: To claim merit and receive reward—how can this satisfy men's hearts?
translations.idiomatic: To claim merit and receive reward—how can this satisfy the hearts of the people?

sentences.zh: 乞立賜罷斥，奪其加恩，為大臣事君不忠者戒。

translations.literal: I beg that he be immediately dismissed and stripped of his added favors, as a warning to great ministers who are unfaithful in serving their ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be dismissed at once and stripped of his added favors, as a warning to great ministers who are unfaithful in serving their ruler.

sentences.zh: 」疏出，東陽涕泣不能辯。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was issued, Dongyang wept and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was issued, Dongyang wept and could not defend himself.

sentences.zh: 帝責芹沽名，令對狀。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Qin for seeking a reputation and ordered him to answer the charges in person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached Qin for courting fame and ordered him to answer the charges in person.

sentences.zh: 芹請罪，停俸三月。

translations.literal: Qin pleaded guilty and had his salary suspended for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Qin pleaded guilty and had his salary suspended for three months.

sentences.zh: 給事中竇明言事下獄，芹疏救之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Dou Ming was imprisoned for remonstrating on state affairs; Qin memorialized to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Dou Ming was imprisoned for remonstrating on affairs of state; Qin submitted a memorial to save him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗馳馬傷，編修王思切諫，坐遠戍。

translations.literal: The emperor once was injured while galloping on horseback; Compiler Wang Si remonstrated sharply and was sentenced to distant exile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was once injured while galloping on horseback; Compiler Wang Si remonstrated sharply and was sentenced to distant exile.

sentences.zh: 芹曰：「彼非諫官尚爾，吾儕可坐視乎！

translations.literal: Qin said: "He was not even a remonstrating official, yet he acted thus—can we of our company sit and watch!"
translations.idiomatic: Qin said: "He was not even a remonstrating official, yet he acted thus—can we simply sit and watch!"

sentences.zh: 」遂上疏曰：「孟子言：『從獸無厭謂之荒』。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "Mencius said: 'To follow beasts without restraint is called dissipation.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial, saying: "Mencius said: 'To follow beasts without restraint is called dissipation.'"

sentences.zh: 老聃曰：『馳騁田獵，使人心發狂』。

translations.literal: Laozi said: 'Galloping in the hunt makes the human heart go mad.'"
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said: 'Galloping in the hunt makes the human heart go mad.'"

sentences.zh: 心狂誌荒，何事不忘？

translations.literal: When the heart is mad and the will dissipated, what affair will not be neglected?
translations.idiomatic: When the heart runs wild and the will dissolves, what affair will not be neglected?

sentences.zh: 皆甚言無益有害也。

translations.literal: Both spoke strongly that it was without benefit and harmful.
translations.idiomatic: Both spoke plainly that such conduct was without benefit and harmful.

sentences.zh: 今輕萬乘之尊，乘危冒險，萬一有不可諱，皇嗣未誕，如宗廟社稷何！

translations.literal: Now you lightly treat the dignity of the ten-thousand-chariot lord, riding danger and courting peril; if by any chance something irreparable should occur and the imperial heir is not yet born, what of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain!
translations.idiomatic: Now you lightly treat the dignity of the Son of Heaven, riding into danger and courting peril; if by any chance something irreparable should occur while the imperial heir is not yet born, what will become of the ancestral temples and the altars of soil and grain!

sentences.zh: 」帝不省。

translations.literal: " The emperor took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 尋出為徽州知府。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out to serve as prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠反，言者以芹家江西，慮賊劫其親屬，取道出徽。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, remonstrators said that because Qin's family was in Jiangxi, they feared the bandits would seize his kin; he should go by way of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, remonstrators noted that Qin's family was in Jiangxi and feared the rebels might seize his relatives; they urged that he travel by way of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 乃改知杭州。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to administer Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore transferred to administer Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 已，復還徽州。

translations.literal: Afterward he returned again to Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he returned again to Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遷浙江海道副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhejiang maritime circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhejiang maritime circuit.

sentences.zh: 歷右參政、右布政使。

translations.literal: He successively served as right administration commissioner and right provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as right administration commissioner and right provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 坐為海道時倭人爭貢誤傷居民，罷歸。

translations.literal: Because while on the maritime circuit Japanese disputing over tribute had mistakenly injured residents, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Because while serving on the maritime circuit Japanese disputing over tribute had mistakenly injured local residents, he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 芹事繼母孝，持身儉素，枲袍糲食終其身。

translations.literal: Qin was filial toward his stepmother, maintained himself in frugal simplicity, and wore hemp robes and coarse food to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Qin was filial toward his stepmother, lived frugally and simply, and wore hemp robes and ate coarse food to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 汪應軫，字子宿，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Yingzhen, style name Zisu, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yingzhen, whose style name was Zisu, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少有誌操。

translations.literal: From youth he had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed resolve and moral integrity.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年成進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he passed as jinshi and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign he passed the jinshi examination and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔將南巡。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict announced that the emperor would tour the south.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year an edict announced that the emperor would tour the south.

sentences.zh: 應軫抗言：「自下詔以來，臣民旁皇，莫有固誌。

translations.literal: Yingzhen remonstrated forcefully: "Since the edict was issued, officials and people have been unsettled, with none holding firm purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen remonstrated forcefully: "Since the edict was issued, officials and commoners alike have been adrift, with none holding firm purpose.

sentences.zh: 臨清以南，率棄業罷市，逃竄山谷。

translations.literal: South of Linqing, all have abandoned their occupations and shut their markets, fleeing into the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: South of Linqing, people have everywhere abandoned their trades and shut their markets, fleeing into the mountains and valleys.

sentences.zh: 茍不即收成命，恐變生不測。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not immediately withdraw the command, I fear unforeseen troubles may arise.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not immediately withdraw the command, I fear unforeseen troubles may arise.

sentences.zh: 昔谷永諫漢成帝，謂：『陛下厭高美之尊號，好匹夫之卑字。

translations.literal: Formerly Gu Yong remonstrated with Emperor Cheng of Han, saying: 'Your Majesty dislikes the lofty and beautiful title of honor and delights in the lowly style of a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Gu Yong remonstrated with Emperor Cheng of Han, saying: 'Your Majesty dislikes the lofty and august title of honor and delights in the lowly style of a common man.

sentences.zh: 數離深宮，挺身晨夜，與群小相逐。

translations.literal: You repeatedly leave the deep palace, thrust yourself forth morning and night, and race with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: You repeatedly leave the inner palace, thrust yourself forth morning and night, and race with petty men.

sentences.zh: 典門戶奉宿衛者，執幹戈而守空宮』。

translations.literal: Those who manage the gates and attend night watch hold weapons and guard an empty palace.'"
translations.idiomatic: Those who manage the gates and attend night watch hold weapons and guard an empty palace.'"

sentences.zh: 其言切中於今。

translations.literal: His words cut directly to the present situation.
translations.idiomatic: His words cut directly to the present situation.

sentences.zh: 夫谷永，諧諛之臣；

translations.literal: Now Gu Yong was a fawning and flattering minister;
translations.idiomatic: Now Gu Yong was a fawning and flattering minister;

sentences.zh: 成帝，庸暗之主。

translations.literal: Chengdi was a mediocre and dim ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng was a mediocre and dim ruler.

sentences.zh: 永言而成帝容之。

translations.literal: Yong spoke and Chengdi accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong spoke, and Emperor Cheng accepted it.

sentences.zh: 豈以陛下聖明，不能俯納直諫哉？

translations.literal: How could it be that Your Majesty, being sage and enlightened, cannot bow to accept straightforward remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Surely Your Majesty, being sage and enlightened, can bow to accept straightforward remonstrance?

sentences.zh: 」疏入，留中。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, it was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, it was kept at court without action.

sentences.zh: 繼復偕修撰舒芬等連章以請。

translations.literal: Thereafter he again joined Compiler Shu Fen and others in successive memorials requesting [withdrawal].
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he again joined Compiler Shu Fen and others in successive memorials requesting withdrawal of the tour.

sentences.zh: 跪闕門，受杖幾斃。

translations.literal: They knelt at the palace gate and were beaten with staves nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: They knelt at the palace gate and were beaten with staves nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 教習竣，擬授給事中。

translations.literal: When their instruction was completed, they were slated to be appointed supervising secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: When their instruction was completed, they were slated to be appointed supervising secretaries.

sentences.zh: 有旨補外，遂出為泗州知州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them assigned outside [the capital], and Yingzhen was sent out as prefect of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them assigned outside the capital, and Yingzhen was sent out as prefect of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 土瘠民惰，不知農桑。

translations.literal: The soil was poor and the people indolent; they did not know agriculture or sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was poor and the people indolent; they knew neither farming nor sericulture.

sentences.zh: 應軫勸之耕，買桑植之。

translations.literal: Yingzhen urged them to plow and bought mulberry trees to plant.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen urged them to plow and bought mulberry trees for planting.

sentences.zh: 募江南女工，教以蠶繅織作。

translations.literal: He recruited women workers from Jiangnan and taught them silkworm rearing, reeling, and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited women workers from Jiangnan and taught them silkworm rearing, reeling, and weaving.

sentences.zh: 由是民足衣食。

translations.literal: Thereby the people had sufficient clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the people came to have sufficient clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 帝方南征，中使驛騷道路。

translations.literal: The emperor was then on his southern expedition; palace envoys disturbed the roads at relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then on his southern expedition, and palace envoys disturbed the roads at every relay station.

sentences.zh: 應軫率壯夫百余人列水次，舟至，即挽之出境。

translations.literal: Yingzhen led more than a hundred strong men to line the riverbank; when a boat arrived, they immediately towed it out of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen led more than a hundred strong men to line the riverbank; when a boat arrived, they immediately towed it out of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 車駕駐南京，命州進美婦善歌吹者數十人。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at Nanjing, he ordered the prefecture to present several dozen beautiful women skilled in song and wind instruments.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage halted at Nanjing, he ordered the prefecture to present several dozen beautiful women skilled in song and wind instruments.

sentences.zh: 應軫言：「州子女荒陋，無以應敕旨。

translations.literal: Yingzhen said: "The women of this prefecture are crude and plain; there are none to answer the imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen said: "The women of this prefecture are crude and plain; there are none fit to answer the imperial command.

sentences.zh: 臣向募有桑婦，請納之宮中，傳受蠶事。

translations.literal: Your subject has previously recruited mulberry-working women; I beg to send them into the palace to transmit the arts of sericulture."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has previously recruited women skilled in sericulture; I beg to send them into the palace to transmit the arts of silkworm raising."

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter thereupon lapsed.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，召為戶科給事中。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, Yingzhen was summoned as supervising secretary of the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, Yingzhen was summoned as supervising secretary of the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 山東礦盜起，掠東昌、兗州，流入畿輔、河南境。

translations.literal: Mining bandits rose in Shandong, plundering Dongchang and Yanzhou and flowing into the capital region and the territory of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Mining bandits rose in Shandong, plundering Dongchang and Yanzhou and spilling into the capital region and Henan.

sentences.zh: 應軫奏言：「弭盜與禦寇不同。

translations.literal: Yingzhen memorialized: "Quelling bandits differs from repelling invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen memorialized: "Quelling bandits differs from repelling invaders.

sentences.zh: 禦寇之法，驅之境外而已。

translations.literal: The method for repelling invaders is merely to drive them beyond the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The method for repelling invaders is merely to drive them beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 若弭盜而縱使出境，是嫁禍於鄰國也。

translations.literal: If in quelling bandits one lets them go out of the borders, that is shifting disaster onto a neighboring state.
translations.idiomatic: If in quelling bandits one lets them escape across the border, that is shifting disaster onto a neighboring region.

sentences.zh: 凡一方有警，不行撲滅，致延蔓他境者，俱宜重論。

translations.literal: Whenever alarm arises in one region and suppression is not carried out, causing it to spread into other regions, all such cases should be heavily punished.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever alarm arises in one region and officials fail to suppress it, allowing trouble to spread into other regions, all such cases should be heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The response approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The response approved it.

sentences.zh: 在科歲餘，所上凡三十余疏，鹹切時弊。

translations.literal: While in the section for more than a year, he submitted in all more than thirty memorials, all penetratingly addressing the abuses of the times.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the section for more than a year, he submitted more than thirty memorials in all, each penetratingly addressing the abuses of the times.

sentences.zh: 以便養，乞改南，遂調南京戶科。

translations.literal: To facilitate caring for his parents, he begged transfer to the south and was therefore reassigned to the Household Section at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: To facilitate caring for his parents, he begged transfer to the south and was reassigned to the Household Section at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼在南京，方議追尊獻皇帝。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E were at Nanjing, then debating posthumous elevation of the Xian Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E were at Nanjing, then debating posthumous elevation of the Jiajing Emperor's father.

sentences.zh: 雅知應軫名，欲倚以自助。

translations.literal: They had long known Yingzhen's reputation and wished to rely on him to assist themselves.
translations.idiomatic: They had long known Yingzhen's reputation and wished to rely on him for support.

sentences.zh: 應軫與議不合，即奏請遵禮經、崇正統，以安人心。

translations.literal: Yingzhen disagreed with their deliberations and immediately memorialized asking that the ritual classics be followed and the legitimate succession honored, to settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen disagreed with their position and immediately memorialized asking that the ritual classics be followed and the legitimate succession honored, to settle the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年春，出為江西僉事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Jiajing he was sent out as assistant administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Jiajing he was sent out as assistant administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 居二年，具疏引疾，不俟命而歸，為巡按所劾。

translations.literal: After two years he submitted a full memorial citing illness, returned home without awaiting orders, and was impeached by the touring censor.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he submitted a full memorial citing illness, returned home without awaiting orders, and was impeached by the touring censor.

sentences.zh: 詔所司逮問。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to arrest and question him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the relevant offices to arrest and question him.

sentences.zh: 應軫自陳親老，鮮兄弟，乞休侍養。

translations.literal: Yingzhen stated in his own defense that his parents were aged, he had few brothers, and begged leave to retire and serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen stated in his own defense that his parents were aged, he had few brothers, and begged leave to retire and serve them.

sentences.zh: 吏部為之請，乃免逮。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized on his behalf, and he was therefore exempted from arrest.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel memorialized on his behalf, and he was therefore exempted from arrest.

sentences.zh: 久之，廷臣交薦，起故官，視江西學政。

translations.literal: After a long time, court officials jointly recommended him; he was restored to his former office and appointed to oversee educational administration in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval, court officials jointly recommended him; he was restored to his former rank and appointed to oversee educational administration in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 父艱歸，病卒。

translations.literal: He returned home on his father's death and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father and died of illness.

sentences.zh: 蕭鳴鳳，字子雝，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Xiao Mingfeng, style name Ziyong, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mingfeng, whose style name was Ziyong, came from Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少從王守仁遊，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Wang Shouren and placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Wang Shouren and placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 正德九年成進士，授御史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhengde he passed as jinshi and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Zhengde reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 副使胡世寧下獄，抗章救之。

translations.literal: When Vice Commissioner Hu Shining was imprisoned, he submitted a forceful memorial to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Commissioner Hu Shining was imprisoned, he submitted a forceful memorial to save him.

sentences.zh: 同官內江高公韶劾王瓊誤邊計，言：「松潘副將吳坤請增設總兵於成都，瓊即以坤任之。

translations.literal: His colleague Gao Gongshao of Neijiang impeached Wang Qiong for errors in frontier strategy, saying: "Songpan Vice Commander Wu Kun requested that a regional commander be newly established at Chengdu, and Qiong immediately appointed Kun to the post.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Gao Gongshao of Neijiang impeached Wang Qiong for errors in frontier strategy, saying: "Songpan Vice Commander Wu Kun requested that a regional commander be newly established at Chengdu, and Qiong immediately appointed Kun to the post.

sentences.zh: 花當本我屬衛，日憑陵。

translations.literal: Huadang was originally our subordinate guard, yet day by day he encroached and bullied.
translations.idiomatic: Huadang was originally our subordinate guard, yet day by day he encroached and bullied us.

sentences.zh: 由本兵非人，致小醜輕中國。

translations.literal: Because the Ministry of War was not in capable hands, petty villains came to despise China.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Ministry of War was not in capable hands, petty foes came to despise the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 」瓊怒，奏訐公韶。

translations.literal: " Qiong was enraged and memorialized to denounce Gongshao.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiong was enraged and memorialized to denounce Gongshao.

sentences.zh: 中旨責公韶陰結外蕃，交通間諜，令首實。

translations.literal: An edict from the inner court reproached Gongshao for secretly allying with foreign tribes and communicating with spies, ordering him to confess the facts first.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from the inner court reproached Gongshao for secretly allying with foreign tribes and communicating with spies, ordering him to confess the facts first.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳳上疏曰：「公韶劾瓊，所論者天下之事。

translations.literal: Mingfeng submitted a memorial saying: "Gongshao impeached Qiong on matters concerning the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfeng submitted a memorial, saying: "Gongshao impeached Qiong on matters concerning the realm.

sentences.zh: 瓊不當逞忿恣辯，以箝諫官口。

translations.literal: Qiong ought not vent his anger and argue at will, thereby gagging the mouths of remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong ought not vent his anger and argue at will, thereby silencing remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 」中旨責鳴鳳黨庇，而謫公韶富民典史。

translations.literal: " An edict from the inner court reproached Mingfeng for factional protection, while Gongshao was demoted to clerk at Fumin.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict from the inner court reproached Mingfeng for factional protection, while Gongshao was demoted to clerk at Fumin.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳳又劾江彬恃寵恣肆，蔓將難圖。

translations.literal: Mingfeng again impeached Jiang Bin for relying on favor and acting wantonly, saying his influence would spread and prove hard to uproot.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfeng again impeached Jiang Bin for relying on imperial favor and acting wantonly, warning that his influence would spread and prove hard to uproot.

sentences.zh: 士論壯之。

translations.literal: Scholarly opinion applauded him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarly opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 尋巡視山海諸關。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he toured the mountain and sea passes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was assigned to inspect the mountain and sea passes.

sentences.zh: 武宗將出塞捕虎，鳴鳳疏諫，因具陳官司掊克，軍民疾苦狀。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was about to go beyond the passes to hunt tigers, Mingfeng memorialized in remonstrance and set forth in detail the extortion of officials and the sufferings of soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor was about to go beyond the passes to hunt tigers, Mingfeng memorialized in remonstrance and set forth in detail the extortion of officials and the sufferings of soldiers and civilians.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 引疾歸。

translations.literal: He cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起督南畿學政。

translations.literal: He was recalled to supervise educational administration in the Southern Metropolitan Region.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to supervise educational administration in the Southern Metropolitan Region.

sentences.zh: 諸生以比前御史陳選，曰「陳，泰山；

translations.literal: The students compared him with the former censor Chen Xuan, saying "Chen is Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: The students compared him with the former censor Chen Xuan, saying "Chen is Mount Tai;

sentences.zh: 蕭，北斗」。

translations.literal: Xiao is the Northern Dipper."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao is the Northern Dipper."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，遷河南副使，仍督學政。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was transferred to vice commissioner of Henan, still supervising educational administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of Henan, while continuing to supervise educational administration.

sentences.zh: 考察拾遺被劾。

translations.literal: In the evaluation for omitted cases he was impeached.
translations.idiomatic: In the evaluation for omitted cases he was impeached.

sentences.zh: 吏部惜其學行，調為湖廣兵備副使。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel valued his learning and conduct and transferred him to vice commissioner for military preparedness in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel valued his learning and conduct and transferred him to vice commissioner for military preparedness in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 明年復改督廣東學政。

translations.literal: The next year he was again reassigned to supervise educational administration in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again reassigned to supervise educational administration in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳳三督學政，廉無私。

translations.literal: Mingfeng thrice supervised educational administration, incorrupt and without private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfeng supervised educational administration three times, incorrupt and without private favor.

sentences.zh: 然性剛狠，以憤撻肇慶知府鄭璋。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and fierce; in anger he had the Zhaoqing prefect Zheng Zhang beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was harsh and fierce; in anger he had the Zhaoqing prefect Zheng Zhang beaten.

sentences.zh: 璋慚恚，投劾去，由是物論大嘩。

translations.literal: Zhang, ashamed and enraged, submitted his resignation and left; thereby public opinion was greatly stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, ashamed and enraged, submitted his resignation and left; public opinion was thereby greatly stirred.

sentences.zh: 八年考察，兩京言官交章論，坐降調。

translations.literal: In the eighth-year evaluation, remonstrating officials of both capitals submitted successive memorials; he was demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth-year evaluation, remonstrating officials of both capitals submitted successive memorials against him; he was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 已，與璋相詆訐。

translations.literal: Afterward he and Zhang mutually slandered and accused each other.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he and Zhang mutually slandered and accused each other.

sentences.zh: 皆下巡按御史逮治。

translations.literal: Both were handed down to the touring censor for arrest and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Both were handed over to the touring censor for arrest and punishment.

sentences.zh: 鳴鳳遂不出。

translations.literal: Mingfeng thereupon did not take office again.
translations.idiomatic: Mingfeng thereupon never took office again.

sentences.zh: 公韶，正德中為御史，嘗劾總兵官郭勛罪。

translations.literal: Gongshao, while censor in the Zhengde reign, once impeached Regional Commander Guo Xun for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshao served as censor during the Zhengde reign and once impeached Regional Commander Guo Xun for crimes.

sentences.zh: 朵顏花當入寇，又劾總兵官遂安伯陳鏸、中官王欣、巡撫王倬，鏸坐解職。

translations.literal: When the Doyan Huadang invaded, he again impeached Regional Commander Chen Yi, Earl of Sui'an, the palace eunuch Wang Xin, and Grand Coordinator Wang Zhuo; Chen was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Doyan leader Huadang invaded, he again impeached Regional Commander Chen Yi, Earl of Sui'an, the palace eunuch Wang Xin, and Grand Coordinator Wang Zhuo; Chen was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，起謫籍。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was raised from the registers of the demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, he was raised from the registers of the demoted.

sentences.zh: 歷右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: He successively served as right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 終戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He ended as right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as right vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 齊之鸞，字瑞卿，桐城人。

translations.literal: Qi Zhiluan, style name Ruiqing, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Zhiluan, whose style name was Ruiqing, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the sixth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin bachelor and appointed supervising secretary of the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，帝將置肆於京城西偏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year the emperor was about to establish shops in the western quarter of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year the emperor was about to establish shops in the western quarter of the capital.

sentences.zh: 之鸞上言：「近聞有花酒鋪之設，或云車駕將臨幸，或云朝廷收其息。

translations.literal: Zhiluan memorialized: "I have recently heard of the establishment of flower-and-wine shops; some say the imperial carriage will visit them, others that the court will collect their profits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan memorialized: "I have recently heard of the establishment of flower-and-wine shops; some say the imperial carriage will visit them, others that the court will collect their profits.

sentences.zh: 陛下貴為天子，富有四海，乃至競錐刀之利，如倡優館舍乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is honored as Son of Heaven and possesses all within the four seas—must you compete for the profit of a knife's point, like an actor's lodging house?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is honored as Son of Heaven and possesses all within the four seas—must you compete for petty profits, like the keeper of an actor's lodging house?"

sentences.zh: 」應州奏捷，帝降敕：「總督軍務威武大將軍總兵官朱壽剿寇有功，宜特加公爵」。

translations.literal: " When Yingzhou reported victory, the emperor issued an edict: "Zhu Shou, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Mighty General, and Regional Commander, has merit in suppressing bandits and should be specially advanced to duke."
translations.idiomatic: " When Yingzhou reported victory, the emperor issued an edict: "Zhu Shou, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs, Mighty General, and Regional Commander, has merit in suppressing bandits and should be specially advanced to duke."

sentences.zh: 制下，舉朝大駭。

translations.literal: When the decree was issued, the whole court was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree was issued, the whole court was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 之鸞偕諸給事中上言：「自古天子亦有親臨戰陣勘定禍亂者，成功之後，不過南面受賀，勒之金石，播之歌頌已耳，未有加爵酬勞，如今日之顛倒者。

translations.literal: Zhiluan joined the supervising secretaries in memorializing: "Since antiquity there have been Sons of Heaven who personally went to the battlefield to settle calamities and disorder; after success they merely faced south to receive congratulations, had it carved in metal and stone, and spread it in song and praise—that was all. Never has there been ennoblement and reward of labor as inverted as today's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan joined the supervising secretaries in memorializing: "Since antiquity there have been emperors who personally went to the battlefield to settle calamities and disorder; after success they merely faced south to receive congratulations, had it carved in metal and stone, and spread it in song and praise—that was all. Never has there been ennoblement and reward as perverse as today's.

sentences.zh: 不知陛下何所取義，為此不祥之舉，以駴天下耳目，貽百世之譏笑也。」

translations.literal: I do not know what principle Your Majesty takes as his guide in performing this inauspicious act, startling the eyes and ears of the realm and bequeathing ridicule for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what principle Your Majesty takes as his guide in performing this inauspicious act, startling the eyes and ears of the realm and bequeathing ridicule for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 未幾，請召還編修王思，給事中張原、陳鼎，御史周廣、高公韶、李熙、徐文華、李穩、施儒、劉寓生，僉事韓邦奇，評事羅僑，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Before long he requested the recall of Compiler Wang Si, Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yuan and Chen Ding, Censors Zhou Guang, Gao Gongshao, Li Xi, Xu Wenhua, Li Wen, Shi Ru, and Liu Yusheng, Assistant Administration Commissioner Han Bangqi, and Reviewing Official Luo Qiao—all were refused.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he requested the recall of Compiler Wang Si, Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yuan and Chen Ding, Censors Zhou Guang, Gao Gongshao, Li Xi, Xu Wenhua, Li Wen, Shi Ru, and Liu Yusheng, Assistant Administration Commissioner Han Bangqi, and Reviewing Official Luo Qiao—all were refused.

sentences.zh: 帝將巡邊，復自稱威武大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to tour the frontier and again styled himself Mighty General.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to tour the frontier and again styled himself Mighty General.

sentences.zh: 御史袁宗儒疏諫，大學士楊廷和、蔣冕、毛紀以去就爭。

translations.literal: Censor Yuan Zongru memorialized in remonstrance; Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji contended by threatening resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Zongru memorialized in remonstrance; Grand Secretaries Yang Tinghe, Jiang Mian, and Mao Ji contended by threatening resignation.

sentences.zh: 之鸞偕同官言：「三臣居師保之重，身系安危，邇者先後稱疾。

translations.literal: Zhiluan joined his colleagues in saying: "The three ministers hold the weighty post of tutor and protector; their persons are bound up with security and peril. Recently they have successively claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan joined his colleagues in saying: "The three ministers hold the weighty post of tutor and protector; their persons are bound up with the dynasty's security. Recently they have successively claimed illness.

sentences.zh: 今六飛臨邊逾月矣，宗廟社稷百官萬姓寄空城中。

translations.literal: Now the six-horse carriage has been on the frontier for more than a month; the ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, the hundred officials, and the myriad people are left in an empty city.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial carriage has been on the frontier for more than a month; the ancestral temples, altars of soil and grain, the hundred officials, and the myriad people are left in an empty city.

sentences.zh: 人心危疑，幾務叢積，復杜門求決去。

translations.literal: Hearts are anxious and doubtful, state affairs pile up in confusion, yet they again shut their doors and seek final departure.
translations.idiomatic: Hearts are anxious and doubtful, state affairs pile up in confusion, yet they again shut their doors and seek final departure.

sentences.zh: 萬一事起倉卒，至於僨敗，三臣將何辭謝天下？

translations.literal: If by any chance trouble should arise in haste and lead to ruin, what words will the three ministers have to answer the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance trouble should arise in haste and lead to ruin, what words will the three ministers have to answer the realm?

sentences.zh: 乞陛下以社稷為重，亟返宸居，與大臣共圖治理。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to take the altars of soil and grain as paramount, swiftly return to the imperial residence, and plan governance together with the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to take the altars of soil and grain as paramount, swiftly return to the imperial residence, and plan governance together with the great ministers.

sentences.zh: 」已而御史李潤等復爭之，卒不省。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Censor Li Run and others again contended, but in the end the emperor took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Censor Li Run and others again contended, but in the end the emperor took no heed.

sentences.zh: 之鸞再遷兵科左給事中。

translations.literal: Zhiluan was again promoted to left supervising secretary of the Military Section.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan was again promoted to left supervising secretary of the Military Section.

sentences.zh: 中官馬永成死，詔授其家九十余人官。

translations.literal: When the palace eunuch Ma Yongcheng died, an edict granted offices to more than ninety of his household.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace eunuch Ma Yongcheng died, an edict granted offices to more than ninety members of his household.

sentences.zh: 之鸞言：「永成貴顯，用事十有余年，兄弟子侄皆高爵美官。

translations.literal: Zhiluan said: "Yongcheng was noble and eminent, wielding power for more than ten years; brothers, sons, and nephews all held high ranks and fine offices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan said: "Yongcheng was noble and eminent, wielding power for more than ten years; brothers, sons, and nephews all held high ranks and fine offices.

sentences.zh: 而其儕復為陳乞，將及百人。

translations.literal: Yet his fellows again petition on his behalf, soon to reach a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his associates again petition on his behalf, soon to reach a hundred persons.

sentences.zh: 永成何功，恩濫如此，恐天下聞而解體也。

translations.literal: What merit had Yongcheng, that favor should overflow thus? I fear that when the realm hears of it, hearts will dissolve.
translations.idiomatic: What merit had Yongcheng, that favor should overflow thus? I fear that when the realm hears of it, hearts will lose all cohesion.

sentences.zh: 」帝將南巡，之鸞偕同官及御史楊秉中等交章力諫。

translations.literal: " The emperor was about to tour the south; Zhiluan joined his colleagues and Censor Yang Bingzhong and others in successive forceful memorials of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was about to tour the south; Zhiluan joined his colleagues and Censor Yang Bingzhong and others in successive forceful memorials of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 章入二日，未報。

translations.literal: Two days after the memorials entered, no response came.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after the memorials were submitted, no response came.

sentences.zh: 之鸞等不知所出，伏闕俟命，自辰至申。

translations.literal: Zhiluan and the others knew not what to do; they knelt at the palace gate awaiting orders from the hour chen to the hour shen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiluan and the others knew not what to do; they knelt at the palace gate awaiting orders from morning until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 帝令中官傳諭，乃退。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a palace eunuch to transmit an edict, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a palace eunuch to transmit an edict, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日托疾免朝，欲以為之鸞等罪。

translations.literal: The next day he pleaded illness to excuse himself from court, intending to make this a crime for Zhiluan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pleaded illness to excuse himself from court, intending to make this a crime for Zhiluan and the others.

sentences.zh: 會諸曹郎黃鞏等聯章力諫，乃止不行。

translations.literal: Just then Section Clerks Huang Gong and others submitted joint memorials of forceful remonstrance, and the tour was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Section Clerks Huang Gong and others submitted joint memorials of forceful remonstrance, and the tour was stopped.

sentences.zh: 然鞏等下獄杖譴，之鸞輩亦不敢救也。

translations.literal: Yet Gong and the others were imprisoned and beaten in punishment; Zhiluan's party also dared not save them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gong and the others were imprisoned and beaten in punishment; Zhiluan's party also dared not save them.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，張忠、許泰等南征，命之鸞偕左給事中祝續從軍紀功。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled, Zhang Zhong, Xu Tai, and others marched south; Zhiluan was ordered to join Left Supervising Secretary Zhu Xu in following the army to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, rebelled, Zhang Zhong, Xu Tai, and others marched south; Zhiluan was ordered to join Left Supervising Secretary Zhu Xu in following the army to record merit.

sentences.zh: 未至，賊已滅。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, the rebels had already been destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, the rebels had already been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 群小忌王守仁，譖毀百端，之鸞力白其誣。

translations.literal: Petty men envied Wang Shouren and slandered him on a hundred counts; Zhiluan forcefully declared the calumny false.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men envied Wang Shouren and slandered him on a hundred counts; Zhiluan forcefully declared the calumny false.

sentences.zh: 忠、泰廣搜逆黨，株引無辜，之鸞多所開釋。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tai broadly searched out rebel partisans and implicated the innocent; Zhiluan released many of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tai broadly searched out rebel partisans and implicated the innocent; Zhiluan secured the release of many.

sentences.zh: 且請蠲田租、停力役、寬逋負，帝頗采納。

translations.literal: He also requested remission of land tax, suspension of corvée labor, and leniency on arrears; the emperor largely adopted these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested remission of land tax, suspension of corvée labor, and leniency on tax arrears; the emperor largely adopted these proposals.

sentences.zh: 初冒徐姓，至是始復焉。

translations.literal: At first he had falsely borne the surname Xu; only now did he restore his own.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had falsely borne the surname Xu; only now did he restore his own surname.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，首上疏言：「祖宗法制，悉紛更於群小。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he first memorialized: "The laws and institutions of the ancestors have all been confused and altered by petty men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, he first memorialized: "The laws and institutions of the ancestors have all been confused and altered by petty men.

sentences.zh: 補救之道，在先定聖誌，次廣言路。

translations.literal: The way to remedy this lies first in fixing the sage resolve, and next in broadening the path of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The way to remedy this lies first in fixing the imperial resolve, and next in broadening the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 先朝元兇雖去，根據盤互，連蔓滋多，猶恐巧相營結，或邀定策之賞，或假迎扈之勞，以取憐固寵。

translations.literal: Although the chief villains of the previous reign are gone, their roots and bases intertwine and spread, growing ever more numerous; I still fear they will craftily league together, some seeking reward for fixing the succession, others borrowing merit for escorting the imperial entourage, to win pity and secure favor.
translations.idiomatic: Although the chief villains of the previous reign are gone, their roots and bases intertwine and spread, growing ever more numerous; I still fear they will craftily league together, some seeking reward for fixing the succession, others borrowing merit for escorting the imperial entourage, to win pity and secure favor.

sentences.zh: 天下事豈堪若輩更壞！

translations.literal: How can affairs under Heaven endure further ruin by such men!
translations.idiomatic: How can affairs under Heaven endure further ruin by such men!

sentences.zh: 言者久遏於權奸，欲吐忠鯁懣憤之氣，必有不顧忌諱，至於逆耳者，在嘉納而優容之。

translations.literal: Remonstrators have long been suppressed by powerful villains; wishing to release loyal and indignant breath, there must be some who disregard taboo and speak to the ear's offense—these should be gladly accepted and generously tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators have long been suppressed by powerful villains; wishing to release loyal and indignant breath, there must be some who disregard taboo and speak harsh truths—these should be gladly accepted and generously tolerated.

sentences.zh: 若稍或抑裁，則小人又乘之以讎忠直。

translations.literal: If there is the slightest suppression, petty men will again seize the chance to take revenge on the loyal and upright.
translations.idiomatic: If there is the slightest suppression, petty men will again seize the chance to take revenge on the loyal and upright.

sentences.zh: 言路一塞，不可復開，大為新政累矣。

translations.literal: Once the path of remonstrance is blocked, it cannot be reopened—this would greatly burden the new administration.
translations.idiomatic: Once the path of remonstrance is blocked, it cannot be reopened—this would greatly burden the new administration.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠舉邇年亂政，盡返其初，中興之烈可以立睹。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly raises up the disorders of recent years and wholly returns to the beginning, the splendor of restoration can be seen at once.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly reverses the disorders of recent years and wholly returns to the beginning, the splendor of restoration can be seen at once.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 又劾許泰及兵部尚書王憲，二人竟獲譴。

translations.literal: He again impeached Xu Tai and Minister of War Wang Xian; both ultimately received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He again impeached Xu Tai and Minister of War Wang Xian; both ultimately received punishment.

sentences.zh: 其秋大計京官，被中傷，謫崇德丞。

translations.literal: That autumn, in the great evaluation of capital officials, he was wounded by slander and demoted to assistant magistrate of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, in the great evaluation of capital officials, he was wounded by slander and demoted to assistant magistrate of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 屢遷寧夏僉事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to assistant administration commissioner of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly transferred to assistant administration commissioner of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 饑民采蓬子為食，之鸞為取二封，一進於帝，一以貽閣臣。

translations.literal: Starving people gathered lotus seeds for food; Zhiluan took two packets, presenting one to the emperor and sending one to the grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Starving people gathered lotus seeds for food; Zhiluan took two packets, presenting one to the emperor and sending one to the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 且言時事可憂者三，可惜者四，語極切。

translations.literal: He also said there were three matters of the times to worry over and four to regret, his words extremely urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He also said there were three matters of the times to worry over and four to regret, his words extremely urgent.

sentences.zh: 帝付之所司。

translations.literal: The emperor handed it to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor handed the memorial to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 時方大修邊墻，之鸞董役。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier walls were being greatly repaired; Zhiluan supervised the labor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the frontier walls were being greatly repaired; Zhiluan supervised the labor.

sentences.zh: 巡撫胡東臯稱其能，舉以自代。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hu Donggao praised his ability and recommended him to succeed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hu Donggao praised his ability and recommended him to succeed himself.

sentences.zh: 歷河南、山東副使。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice commissioner of Henan and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as vice commissioner of Henan and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 召為順天府丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未行，盜發，留鎮撫。

translations.literal: Before he departed, bandits rose; he was retained to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Before he departed, bandits rose; he was retained to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 尋擢河南按察使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 袁宗儒，字醇夫，雄縣人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zongru, style name Chunfu, was a native of Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zongru, whose style name was Chunfu, came from Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as a censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年冬，帝在大同，以郊祀將回鑾，既而復止。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, winter, the emperor was at Datong; because of the suburban sacrifice he was about to return the imperial carriage, but then stopped again.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year, the emperor was at Datong and was about to return to the capital for the suburban sacrifice, but then halted again.

sentences.zh: 宗儒率同官力諫。

translations.literal: Zongru led his fellow officials in forceful remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru led his colleagues in a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，孝貞純皇后將葬，帝還京。

translations.literal: The next summer, as Empress Xiaozhenchun was about to be buried, the emperor returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer, as Empress Xiaozhenchun was to be interred, the emperor returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 宗儒等復引災異，力請罷皇店，遣邊兵，既又諫帝巡邊。

translations.literal: Zongru and others again cited portents and omens, strongly requesting the abolition of imperial shops and the dispatch of border troops homeward; afterward they also remonstrated against the emperor's frontier tour.
translations.idiomatic: Zongru and his colleagues again invoked celestial omens, urgently calling for the abolition of the imperial shops and the return of frontier troops, and then remonstrated against the emperor's planned border tour.

sentences.zh: 語極危切。

translations.literal: Their language was extremely urgent and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Their words were piercingly urgent.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received a response.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no answer to any of them.

sentences.zh: 擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Review at the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年爭「大禮」，廷杖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing, disputing the "Great Rites," he suffered beating at court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing, during the Great Rites controversy, he was beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 歷官右僉都御史，巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: He successively served as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and served as grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書桂萼議宗儒改調，遂解職歸。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Gui E proposed transferring Zongru, whereupon he resigned his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Personnel Gui E proposed transferring him elsewhere, Zongru resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起鄖陽，改山東。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve at Yunyang, then transferred to Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was recalled to Yunyang, then reassigned to Shandong.

sentences.zh: 坐屬吏振饑無術，不能覺察，罷免。

translations.literal: Because a subordinate lacked effective famine-relief methods and he failed to detect it, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed after a subordinate bungled famine relief and he had failed to catch the problem.

sentences.zh: 以薦起左副都御史。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was restored to office as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended back to service, he was appointed Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕承天，還京卒。

translations.literal: He accompanied the imperial retinue to Chengtian and died on returning to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While escorting the emperor to Chengtian, he died on the journey back to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 許相卿，字伯臺，海寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Xiangqing, style name Baitai, was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiangqing, whose style name was Baitai, came from Haining.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor acceded, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of War bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor took the throne, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of War bureau.

sentences.zh: 宦官張銳、張忠有罪論死，帝復寬之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Zhang Rui and Zhang Zhong, found guilty and sentenced to death, were again granted leniency by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Zhang Rui and Zhang Zhong had been convicted and sentenced to death, but the emperor pardoned them again.

sentences.zh: 給事中顧濟疏爭，帝下所司議，卒欲寬其死。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Gu Ji memorialized in protest; the emperor referred the matter to the relevant offices for deliberation, ultimately intending to spare them from death.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Gu Ji submitted a memorial in protest, but the emperor referred the case to the relevant offices and still intended to spare them from execution.

sentences.zh: 相卿言：「天下望陛下為孝皇，陛下奈何自處以正德？

translations.literal: Xiangqing said: "All under Heaven look to Your Majesty to be like the Hongzhi Emperor—how can Your Majesty conduct yourself as in the Zhengde reign?
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqing said: "The people look to Your Majesty to rule as the Hongzhi Emperor did—why conduct yourself as the Zhengde Emperor did?

sentences.zh: 」帝議加興獻帝皇號，相卿復爭之。

translations.literal: " When the emperor contemplated conferring an imperial title on the Xingxian Emperor, Xiangqing again remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor proposed granting his father the Xingxian Emperor an imperial title, Xiangqing remonstrated again.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年詔蔭中官張欽義子李賢為錦衣世襲指揮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, an edict ennobled Li Xian, the adopted son of the eunuch Zhang Qin, as hereditary commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, an edict made Li Xian—the adopted son of the eunuch Zhang Qin—a hereditary commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 相卿言：「于謙子冕止錦衣千戶，王守仁子正憲止錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: Xiangqing said: "Yu Qian's son Mian received only the rank of qianhu in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, and Wang Shouren's son Zhengxian only baihu in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqing said: "Yu Qian's son Mian was granted only the rank of qianhu in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, and Wang Shouren's son Zhengxian only the rank of baihu.

sentences.zh: 賢中官廝養，反過之。

translations.literal: Li Xian was a eunuch's fostered servant, yet his reward surpassed theirs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian was nothing but a eunuch's fosterling, yet he was rewarded above them.

sentences.zh: 忠勛大臣裔曾不若近幸奴，殉國勤事之臣誰不解體？

translations.literal: The descendants of loyal and meritorious grand ministers were not even the equal of a favored attendant's slave—what official who died for the state or toiled in duty would not lose heart?
translations.idiomatic: The heirs of loyal, meritorious ministers were outranked by a favorite's lackey—what servant of the state would not be disheartened?

sentences.zh: 部臣彭澤、科臣許復禮、安磐相繼言之，悉拒不納。

translations.literal: The ministry official Peng Ze, the censorate official Xu Fuli, and An Pan spoke in succession, but all were firmly rejected and not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Ze of the ministries, Xu Fuli of the censorate, and An Pan spoke in turn, but the emperor refused to accept any of it.

sentences.zh: 毋乃重內侍而輕士大夫哉！」

translations.literal: Might this not mean valuing inner attendants above and slighting scholar-officials below!"
translations.idiomatic: Are you not placing eunuchs above the scholar-official class?!"

sentences.zh: 尋復言：「天下政權出於一則治，二三則亂；

translations.literal: Soon he again said: "When authority under Heaven issues from one source, there is order; from two or three, there is chaos;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he memorialized again: "When authority under Heaven flows from a single source, the realm is governed; when it flows from two or three, the realm falls into disorder;

sentences.zh: 公卿大夫參議則治，匪人僭幹則亂。

translations.literal: when high ministers participate in deliberation, there is order; when unworthy men usurp and meddle, there is chaos.
translations.idiomatic: when grand ministers share in deliberation, there is order; when unworthy men usurp power, there is chaos.

sentences.zh: 陛下繼統之初，登用老成，嘉納忠讜，裁抑僥幸，竄殛憸邪，可謂明且剛矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's succession, you employed seasoned men, gladly accepted loyal remonstrance, restrained favor-seekers, banished and punished the crooked—this could be called both enlightened and firm.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of your reign, you employed seasoned statesmen, welcomed loyal counsel, checked favor-seekers, and banished the wicked—you seemed both clear-sighted and resolute.

sentences.zh: 曾未再期，偏聽私昵，秕政亟行，明少蔽，剛少遜，操權未得其術，而陰伺旁竊者得居中制之。

translations.literal: Before two years had passed, partial listening to private intimates set in, defective policies were swiftly enacted, enlightenment was somewhat obscured, firmness somewhat yielding; the art of wielding power was not yet mastered, and those who watched from the shadows and stole power in from the side were able to take central control.
translations.idiomatic: Before two years had passed, you listened only to intimates, bad policies multiplied, your clarity dimmed and your resolve softened, you had not yet mastered how to wield power—and men who schemed in the shadows had seized control from the center.

sentences.zh: 如崔文以左道罔上，師保臺諫言之而不聽。

translations.literal: For example, Cui Wen used heterodox ways to deceive his superiors; tutors, mentors, and censorate remonstrators spoke but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Wen deceived the throne with sorcery, yet though tutors and censorate officials remonstrated, you would not listen.

sentences.zh: 羅洪載守職逮系，廷臣疏七十上而不行。

translations.literal: Luo Hongzai, performing his duty, was arrested and bound; court officials submitted seventy memorials, yet nothing was done.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongzai was arrested simply for doing his duty, and though court officials submitted seventy memorials on his behalf, nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 近又庇崔文奴奪法司之守，斥林俊以違旨，怒言官之奏擾。

translations.literal: Recently you again sheltered Cui Wen's slave, seizing the guard duty of the judicial offices; dismissed Lin Jun for violating the imperial will, and grew angry at supervising censors' memorials as a disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Recently you shielded Cui Wen's slave, stripping the judiciary of its prerogatives, dismissed Lin Jun for disobedience, and grew angry at censorial memorials as mere annoyance.

sentences.zh: 事涉中人，曲降溫旨，犯法不罪，請乞必從。

translations.literal: When matters involved eunuchs, you issued gentle edicts; lawbreakers went unpunished, and pleas and requests were always granted.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever eunuchs were involved, you issued conciliatory edicts—crimes went unpunished and every petition was granted.

sentences.zh: 此與正德朝何異哉！

translations.literal: How is this different from the Zhengde reign!
translations.idiomatic: How does this differ from the Zhengde reign?!

sentences.zh: 俊，國之望也，其去誌決矣。

translations.literal: Lin Jun is the nation's hope; his departure shows his resolve is firm.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun is a pillar of the state, and his resignation signals that his mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 俊去，類俊者必不留。

translations.literal: When Lin Jun goes, those like Lin Jun will surely not remain.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lin Jun goes, others like him will not stay either.

sentences.zh: 陛下將與二三近習私人共理天下乎？

translations.literal: Will Your Majesty govern all under Heaven together with two or three intimate favorites and private confidants?
translations.idiomatic: Will you run the empire with a handful of personal favorites?

sentences.zh: 今日天下，與先朝異。

translations.literal: The realm today differs from the previous reign.
translations.idiomatic: The realm today is not what it was under the previous emperor.

sentences.zh: 武宗時，勢已阽危，然元氣猶壯，調劑適宜，可以立起。

translations.literal: Under the Wuzong Emperor, the situation was already perilously endangered, yet the vital force was still robust; with suitable restorative measures, recovery could come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wuzong Emperor the state was near collapse, yet its vital force was still strong—with the right remedies it could have been restored at once.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why was that?

sentences.zh: 承孝宗之澤也。

translations.literal: Because it inherited the beneficence of the Hongzhi Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because it still drew on the legacy of the Hongzhi Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今日病雖稍蘇，而元氣已竭，調劑無方，將至不起。

translations.literal: Today, though the illness has slightly eased, the vital force is already exhausted; with no effective remedy, recovery will soon be impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Today the symptoms have eased slightly, but the vital force is spent—without effective remedy, the patient will not recover.

sentences.zh: 何也？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 承武宗之亂也。

translations.literal: Because it inherits the disorder of the Wuzong Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because it inherits the chaos left by the Wuzong Emperor.

sentences.zh: 伏願深察亂機，收還政柄，取文輩置之重典。

translations.literal: I humbly pray that Your Majesty deeply examine the sources of disorder, reclaim governmental authority, and subject Wen and his ilk to severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to discern the roots of disorder, reclaim the reins of power, and punish Wen and his like with the full severity of the law.

sentences.zh: 然後務學親賢，去讒遠色，延訪忠言，深恤民隱。

translations.literal: Then devote yourself to learning, draw close to the worthy, remove slanderers, keep away from sensual indulgence, seek out loyal counsel, and deeply comfort the people's hidden distress.
translations.idiomatic: Then study earnestly, keep worthy men close, banish slanderers, shun sensual indulgence, seek loyal counsel, and deeply relieve the people's hidden suffering.

sentences.zh: 務使宮府一體，上下一心，而後天下可為也。

translations.literal: Strive to make palace and government a single body and superiors and subordinates of one mind—only then can affairs under Heaven be managed.
translations.idiomatic: Strive to unite the palace and the administration, align rulers and ruled—and only then can the realm be governed.

sentences.zh: 」同官趙漢等亦皆以文為言，帝卒不聽。

translations.literal: " His colleagues Zhao Han and others also spoke concerning Wen, but the emperor ultimately would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Colleagues such as Zhao Han also spoke against Wen, but the emperor still refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以給事中李學曾、章僑、主事林應驄皆言事奪俸，復上疏諫。

translations.literal: Before long, because the supervising secretaries Li Xuezeng and Zhang Qiao and the director Lin Yingcong all had their salaries stripped for speaking on affairs of state, he again submitted a memorial in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, after Supervising Secretaries Li Xuezeng and Zhang Qiao and Director Lin Yingcong all lost salary for speaking out, he submitted another remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 指帝氣驕誌怠，甘蹈過愆。

translations.literal: He pointed to the emperor's proud spirit and slack will, willing to repeat past faults.
translations.idiomatic: He accused the emperor of arrogance and complacency, willing to repeat past mistakes.

sentences.zh: 詞甚切。

translations.literal: His language was very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: His words were blisteringly sharp.

sentences.zh: 為給事三年，所言皆不聽，遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: Having served three years as supervising secretary, none of his counsel was heeded, so he resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After three years as supervising secretary, with none of his advice heeded, he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔養病三年以上不赴都者，悉落職閑住，相卿遂廢。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict declared that all who had been on sick leave for more than three years without returning to the capital would be stripped of office and left idle; Xiangqing was thus dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, an edict dismissed all officials who had been on sick leave for more than three years without returning to the capital; Xiangqing was therefore forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 夏言故與同僚相善，既秉政，招之，謝弗應。

translations.literal: Xia Yan had formerly been on good terms with his colleagues; once he held power, he summoned him, but Xiangqing declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan, once his colleague and now in power, summoned him back, but Xiangqing politely refused.

sentences.zh: 顧濟，字舟卿，昆山人。

translations.literal: Gu Ji, style name Zhouqing, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Ji, whose style name was Zhouqing, came from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier, then promoted to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Justice bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a courier and was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Justice bureau.

sentences.zh: 武宗自南都還，臥病豹房，惟江彬等侍。

translations.literal: The Wuzong Emperor, returning from the Southern Capital, lay ill in the Leopard Quarter, with only Jiang Bin and others in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong Emperor returned from Nanjing, he lay ill in the Leopard Quarter, attended only by Jiang Bin and his clique.

sentences.zh: 濟言：「陛下孤寄於外，兩宮隔絕，骨肉日疏。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Your Majesty dwells in isolation abroad; the two palaces are cut off from each other, and flesh and blood grow daily more estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said: "Your Majesty dwells alone far from court; the two palaces are cut off from each other, and your kin grow more distant by the day.

sentences.zh: 所恃以為安者，果何人哉？

translations.literal: On whom do you truly rely for your safety?
translations.idiomatic: On whom do you truly rely to feel secure?

sentences.zh: 漢高帝臥病數日，樊噲排闥，警以趙高之事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Han lay ill for several days, Fan Kuai burst through the gate and warned him with the affair of Zhao Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu of Han fell ill, Fan Kuai forced his way in and warned him with the example of Zhao Gao.

sentences.zh: 今群臣中豈無噲憂者！

translations.literal: Among the ministers today, is there truly no one like Fan Kuai who is full of worry!
translations.idiomatic: Surely there are ministers today as anxious as Fan Kuai was!

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎擇廷臣更番入直，起居動息鹹使與聞。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would carefully choose court officials to attend in rotation on duty, so that all your movements and rest are known to them.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to select court officials to attend in rotation, so that your every movement and rest is known to trustworthy men.

sentences.zh: 一切淫巧戲劇，傷生敗德之事，悉行屏絕，則保養有道，聖躬自安。

translations.literal: Let all licentious clever tricks, performances, and matters that harm the body and ruin virtue be wholly barred; then there will be proper means of nurturing health, and Your Majesty's sacred person will naturally be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Ban every lewd diversion and performance that harms body and character—then you will be properly cared for and Your Majesty's person will be secure.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 再逾月而帝崩。

translations.literal: Another month passed, and the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Little more than a month later, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位之月，濟上疏曰：「陛下踐阼，除弊納諫，臣民踴躍，思見德化之成。

translations.literal: In the month the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Ji submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has taken the throne, removed abuses, and accepted remonstrance; officials and people leap with joy, longing to see virtuous transformation fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the month the Jiajing Emperor took the throne, Ji submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has ascended the throne, rooting out abuses and welcoming remonstrance; officials and people rejoice, eager to see your virtuous rule take full shape.

sentences.zh: 然立法非難，守法為難；

translations.literal: Yet making laws is not difficult; keeping to the laws is difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Yet enacting laws is not hard—upholding them is hard;

sentences.zh: 聽諫非難，樂諫為難。

translations.literal: hearing remonstrance is not difficult; delighting in remonstrance is difficult.
translations.idiomatic: hearing remonstrance is not hard—welcoming it gladly is hard.

sentences.zh: 今新政所厘，多不便於奸豪權悻。

translations.literal: The new policies now being rectified are mostly inconvenient to villainous magnates and power-seeking favorites.
translations.idiomatic: The reforms you have begun mostly inconvenience corrupt magnates and powerful favorites.

sentences.zh: 臣恐盤據既深，玩縱未已，非依怙宮闈，必請托左右。

translations.literal: I fear that since their entrenchment is already deep and their lax indulgence has not yet ceased, they must either rely on the inner palace or petition through those at Your Majesty's side.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that, deeply entrenched and still unrestrained, they will either lean on the inner palace or press their case through your inner circle.

sentences.zh: 持法不固，則此輩將叢聚而壞之。

translations.literal: If the laws are not firmly upheld, these men will gather in clusters and ruin them.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not hold firm to the law, they will gather and undermine it.

sentences.zh: 此守法之難也。

translations.literal: This is the difficulty of keeping to the laws.
translations.idiomatic: That is the difficulty of upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 唐太宗貞觀初，每導群臣使言。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenguan reign, Emperor Taizong of Tang always guided his ministers to speak.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhenguan reign, Emperor Taizong of Tang constantly encouraged his ministers to speak freely.

sentences.zh: 及至晚年，諫者乃多忤旨。

translations.literal: By his later years, those who remonstrated often went against the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, however, remonstrators often found themselves at odds with the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下首辟言路，臣工靡不因事納忠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty first opened the path of remonstrance, and officials have none failed to offer loyal counsel on matters as they arise.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty first opened the channels of remonstrance, and officials have seized every occasion to offer loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 高遠者似涉於迂闊，切直者或過於犯顏。

translations.literal: Those whose words are far-reaching seem to touch on the broad and impractical; those who are direct and blunt may go too far in offending your countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel that reaches far may seem impractical; counsel that is blunt may seem to insult your dignity.

sentences.zh: 若怒其犯顏，其言必不入；

translations.literal: If you grow angry at those who offend your countenance, their words will surely not enter;
translations.idiomatic: If you grow angry at blunt speakers, their words will never reach you;

sentences.zh: 視為迂闊，則計必不行。

translations.literal: if you regard them as broad and impractical, their plans will surely not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: if you dismiss them as impractical, their proposals will never be acted on.

sentences.zh: 此樂諫之難也。

translations.literal: This is the difficulty of delighting in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: That is the difficulty of truly welcoming remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 」尋復言：「內臣張雄、張銳等，詿誤先帝，業已逮治，又獲寬假。

translations.literal: " Soon he again said: "The inner officials Zhang Xiong, Zhang Rui, and others misled the former emperor; they had already been arrested for punishment, yet again received leniency.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon memorialized again: "The eunuchs Zhang Xiong and Zhang Rui misled the late emperor; though already arrested for trial, they have again been granted leniency.

sentences.zh: 願斷以大義。

translations.literal: I wish that they be cut off according to great principle.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to judge them by the standards of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 俾無所售奸。

translations.literal: So that they have no place to peddle their wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: So that they can no longer peddle their schemes.

sentences.zh: 」帝頗嘉納。

translations.literal: " The emperor rather praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor responded favorably.

sentences.zh: 既又劾司禮蕭敬黨庇銳等，而三法司會訊依違，無大臣節。

translations.literal: He then again impeached the Director of Ceremonials Xiao Jing for party favoritism toward Rui and others, while the three judicial offices, meeting to interrogate, wavered—showing no integrity befitting grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Director of Ceremonials Xiao Jing for shielding Rui and others, while the three highest judicial offices hedged in their joint inquiry, lacking the backbone expected of grand ministers.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 帝欲加興獻帝皇號，濟言不可。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to confer an imperial title on the Xingxian Emperor, Ji said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proposed granting his father the Xingxian Emperor an imperial title, Ji opposed it.

sentences.zh: 尋請侍養歸，越數年卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he requested leave to return home and care for his parents; several years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to go home to care for his parents and died several years later.

sentences.zh: 子章誌，嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: His son Zhang Zhi passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhi, his son, received his jinshi degree in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 累官南京兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served up to Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to serve as Vice Minister of War in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 奏減進奉馬快船額，南都人祀之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the quota for tribute couriers' horse-and-express boats; the people of the Southern Capital enshrined him in worship.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to cut the quota for tribute express boats, and the people of Nanjing enshrined him in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 章僑，字處仁，蘭溪人。

translations.literal: Zhang Qiao, style name Churen, was a native of Lanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qiao, whose style name was Churen, came from Lanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。
