translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the twelfth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a courier.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年擢禮科給事中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was promoted to supervising secretary of the Ministry of Rites bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites bureau.

sentences.zh: 疏劾中官蕭敬、芮景賢等。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial impeaching the eunuchs Xiao Jing, Rui Jingxian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized impeaching the eunuchs Xiao Jing, Rui Jingxian, and others.

sentences.zh: 又言：「三代以下正學莫如朱熹。

translations.literal: He again said: "Since the Three Dynasties, there has been no orthodox learning like that of Zhu Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Since the Three Dynasties, no scholar has embodied orthodox learning better than Zhu Xi.

sentences.zh: 近有聰明才智，倡異學以號召，天下好高務名者靡然宗之。

translations.literal: Recently there have been men of clever intelligence who promote heterodox learning to rally followers; throughout the realm those who admire what is lofty and pursue fame have invariably turned to them as a school.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, clever men have been preaching unorthodox doctrines and drawing crowds; scholars hungry for reputation have flocked to them.

sentences.zh: 取陸九淵之簡便，詆朱熹為支離。

translations.literal: They take Lu Jiuyuan's simplicity and convenience, and denounce Zhu Xi as fragmentary and pedantic.
translations.idiomatic: They embrace Lu Jiuyuan's shortcut to enlightenment while dismissing Zhu Xi as tedious and overcomplicated.

sentences.zh: 乞行天下，痛為禁革。

translations.literal: I beg that this be promulgated throughout the realm and sternly prohibited and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that such teachings be banned throughout the empire without delay.

sentences.zh: 」御史梁世驃亦言之。

translations.literal: " Censor Liang Shipiao also spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor Liang Shipiao made the same argument.

sentences.zh: 帝為下詔申禁。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict reiterating the prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor responded with an edict reinforcing the ban.

sentences.zh: 尋又請依祖宗故事，早朝班退，許百官以次啟事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he again requested that, according to ancestral precedent, after the early audience the ranks withdraw and officials be permitted to present business in turn.
translations.idiomatic: He soon proposed restoring the old custom of allowing officials, after the morning audience, to report matters to the throne in turn.

sentences.zh: 經筵日講，賜清問，密勿大臣勤召對。

translations.literal: Daily lectures at the Classics Colloquium, grants of clear inquiry, and frequent summoning of close ministers for imperial audience.
translations.idiomatic: He urged daily Classics Colloquium lectures, open questioning by the emperor, and regular private audiences with senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 又簡儒臣十數人，更番直便殿，以備咨訪。

translations.literal: He also selected more than ten Confucian officials to rotate duty in the convenience hall, to be ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended that a dozen scholar-officials rotate through duty in the side hall, available for the emperor's consultation.

sentences.zh: 上納其言，而不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words but could not put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor acknowledged the proposal but never acted on it.

sentences.zh: 奸人何淵請立世室於太廟東北，僑力言其不可。

translations.literal: The schemer He Yuan requested establishing a Shishi chamber northeast of the Imperial Ancestral Temple; Qiao forcefully argued it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the schemer He Yuan proposed building a Shishi chamber northeast of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Qiao remonstrated vigorously against it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又言：「添設織造內臣，貪橫殊甚。

translations.literal: Before long, he again said: "The newly added eunuchs for imperial weaving manufacture are extremely greedy and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he wrote: "The eunuchs added to oversee imperial textile manufacture are flagrantly greedy and abusive.

sentences.zh: 行戶至廢產鬻子以償。

translations.literal: Contract households have even abandoned their estates and sold their children to pay debts.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving households have been driven to ruin their property and sell their children to meet demands.

sentences.zh: 惟急停革，與天下更始。

translations.literal: I urge immediate halt and abolition, so the realm may have a fresh beginning.
translations.idiomatic: They must be abolished at once so the empire can begin anew.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，不省。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, it was not reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was received but ignored.

sentences.zh: 又因條列營務，劾定國公徐光祚、陽武侯薛倫不職，倫遂解任。

translations.literal: He also, listing military affairs in detail, impeached Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo and Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lun for dereliction of duty; Xue Lun was then relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: In a detailed account of military administration he impeached Duke of Dingguo Xu Guangzuo and Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lun for neglect of duty; Xue Lun was promptly removed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋請斥張璁、霍韜等，不聽。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he requested expulsion of Zhang Cong, Huo Tao, and others; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He soon urged that Zhang Cong, Huo Tao, and their faction be dismissed, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 孝陵司香谷大用乞還京治疾。

translations.literal: Gu Dayong, keeper of incense at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, requested return to the capital to treat illness.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Dayong, who tended incense at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, petitioned to return to Beijing for medical treatment.

sentences.zh: 僑言：「大用初連逆瑾，後引寧、彬，樹『八黨』之兇，釀十六年之禍，至先帝不得正其終。

translations.literal: Qiao said: "Dayong at first associated with the rebel eunuch Liu Jin, later introduced Ning and Bin, established the villainy of the 'Eight Cliques,' and brewed sixteen years of calamity, until the late emperor could not meet a proper end.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao wrote: "Dayong first conspired with the rebel eunuch Liu Jin, then brought in Qian Ning and Jiang Bin, raised the notorious 'Eight Cliques,' and set in motion sixteen years of ruin until our late emperor died before his time.

sentences.zh: 若不早遏絕，恐乘間伺隙，群兇競起，不至復亂天下不止。

translations.literal: If not checked early, I fear they will seize intervals and watch for openings; the band of villains will compete to rise, and will not stop short of throwing the realm into chaos again.
translations.idiomatic: Unless he is stopped now, they will watch for their chance, the whole villainous crew will rise together, and the empire will be plunged into turmoil once more.

sentences.zh: 」章下所司。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the appropriate departments.

sentences.zh: 吳廷舉請召家居大臣議禮，僑劾其陰附邪說。

translations.literal: Wu Tingju requested summoning grand ministers at home to discuss rites; Qiao impeached him for secretly attaching himself to heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Tingju proposed summoning retired grand ministers to debate the rites controversy, Qiao impeached him for secretly siding with the heterodox faction.

sentences.zh: 孟秋時享太廟，帝遣京山侯崔元。

translations.literal: At the autumn season-offering in the seventh month at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the emperor dispatched Duke of Jingshan Cui Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: For the midsummer seasonal offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the emperor sent Duke of Jingshan Cui Yuan in his place.

sentences.zh: 僑言：「奉命臨時，倉皇就位，誠敬何存？

translations.literal: Qiao said: "Receiving orders at the last moment and hurrying into position—in what does sincerity and reverence remain?
translations.idiomatic: Qiao protested: "Sent at the last minute to stand in for the emperor—where is the sincerity such a rite demands?

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，奪其俸二月。

translations.literal: " The emperor was angry and stripped him of two months' salary.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was enraged and withheld two months of his salary.

sentences.zh: 歷禮科左給事中。

translations.literal: He served through as Left Supervising Secretary of the Ministry of Rites bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve as Left Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Rites bureau.

sentences.zh: 出知衡州府，終福建布政使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Hengzhou Prefecture and ended as Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Hengzhou and eventually rose to serve as Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 余珊，字德輝，桐城人。

translations.literal: Yu Shan, style name Dehui, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shan, styled Dehui, came from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He passed as jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the third year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，擢御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a courier and was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 庶吉士許成名等罷教習，留翰林者十七人。

translations.literal: Hanlin Bachelor-designates such as Xu Chengming were dismissed from instructorship; seventeen remained in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Hanlin Bachelor-designates including Xu Chengming were removed as instructors, seventeen were still kept on in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 珊以為濫，疏論之。

translations.literal: Shan regarded this as excessive and submitted a memorial discussing it.
translations.idiomatic: Shan considered the retention excessive and memorialized against it.

sentences.zh: 語侵內閣，不納。

translations.literal: His language impinged on the Grand Secretariat; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His criticism reached the Grand Secretariat and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，疏陳弊政，極指義子、西僧之謬。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace burned, he submitted a memorial laying out maladministration and sharply pointing out the errors of adopted sons and Western monks.
translations.idiomatic: After the Qianqing Palace burned, he memorialized on abuses in government, denouncing especially the folly of imperial adoptive sons and Tibetan monks.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽長蘆，發中官奸利事。

translations.literal: While inspecting salt at Changlu, he exposed eunuchs' corrupt profiteering.
translations.idiomatic: On a salt-inspection tour of Changlu, he uncovered eunuch profiteering schemes.

sentences.zh: 為所誣，械系詔獄，謫安陸判官。

translations.literal: He was slandered by them, shackled and imprisoned in the Imperial Prison, and demoted to assistant magistrate of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Framed by his accusers, he was clapped in irons in the Imperial Prison and demoted to assistant magistrate of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 移知澧州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to serve as prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，擢江西僉事，討平梅花峒賊。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended, he was promoted to Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner and pacified the Meihua Cave bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, he was promoted to Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner and put down the bandits of Meihua Cave.

sentences.zh: 遷四川副使，備兵威、茂。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Sichuan Vice Commissioner, guarding troops at Wei and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Sichuan Vice Commissioner with military responsibility for the Wei and Mao regions.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年二月應詔陳十漸，其略曰：

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year of Jiajing, responding to an imperial summons, he laid out the Ten Gradual Declines; the summary reads:
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year of Jiajing, answering an imperial call for memorials, he presented his "Ten Gradual Declines"; in summary:

sentences.zh: 陛下有堯、舜、湯、武之資，而無稷、契、伊、周之佐，致時事漸不克終者有十。

translations.literal: Your Majesty possesses the endowment of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, yet lacks the assistants of Ji, Qi, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou—thereby causing current affairs gradually to fail of completion; there are ten such trends.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has the makings of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wu, but not ministers of the caliber of Ji, Qi, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou—and ten creeping failures now threaten to undo what you have begun.

sentences.zh: 正德間，逆瑾專權，假子亂政，不知紀綱為何物，幸陛下起而振之。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde era, the rebel Jin monopolized power, adopted sons threw governance into chaos, and no one knew what institutional order meant—fortunately Your Majesty arose and revived it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Liu Jin seized power, imperial favorites ran wild, and law and order collapsed—until Your Majesty restored the regime.

sentences.zh: 未幾而事樂因循，政多茍簡，名實乖謬，宮府異同，紛泄沓。

translations.literal: Before long affairs took comfort in procrastination, governance was mostly perfunctory, names and realities diverged, palace and government differed, and confusion spread everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet soon the court drifted back into inertia, policy grew careless, word and deed parted company, palace and government fell out of step, and disorder spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 以為在朝廷而不在朝廷，以為在宮省而不在宮省，遂至天子以其心為心，百官萬民亦各以其心為心。

translations.literal: Some thought they were at court when they were not at court, thought they were in the palace offices when they were not—until the Son of Heaven took his own heart as his heart, and officials and the myriad people each took their own hearts as their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers behaved as if they governed when they did not, as if they served the throne when they did not—until even the emperor followed his private inclinations, and every official and subject did the same.

sentences.zh: 此紀綱之頹，其漸一也。

translations.literal: This is the decline of institutional order—the first gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first gradual decline: the collapse of institutional order.

sentences.zh: 正德間，士大夫寡廉鮮恥，趨附權門，幸陛下起而作之。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, scholar-officials lacked integrity and shame and rushed to attach themselves to powerful houses—fortunately Your Majesty arose and reformed this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, officials lost their sense of honor and shame and flocked to powerful patrons—until Your Majesty set out to reform them.

sentences.zh: 乃今則前日之去者復來，來者不去。

translations.literal: Yet now those who left yesterday have returned, and those who came have not gone.
translations.idiomatic: Now the men who were driven out have come back, and those who returned refuse to leave.

sentences.zh: 自夫浮沈一世之人擢掌銓衡，首取軟美脂韋。

translations.literal: Since men who drifted through a lifetime were elevated to control the Board of Personnel, they first select the soft, fair, and pliant.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since time-servers were put in charge of appointments, the soft, smooth, and pliable have been favored above all.

sentences.zh: 重富貴薄名檢者，列之有位，致諛佞成風，廉恥道薄。

translations.literal: Those who value wealth and honor and slight reputation and self-restraint are ranked in office, causing flattery and sycophancy to become the fashion and the way of integrity and shame to grow thin.
translations.idiomatic: Men who prize wealth and rank over decency have been seated in office, until flattery has become custom and shame has all but vanished.

sentences.zh: 甚者侯伯專糾彈，罷吏議禮樂。

translations.literal: At the extreme, marquises and earls monopolize impeachment, and dismissed officials debate rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: At worst, noblemen have taken it upon themselves to lodge impeachments, and dismissed officials to dictate ritual policy.

sentences.zh: 市門復開，賈販仍舊。

translations.literal: The market gates have opened again; peddlers continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: The gates of office are open for sale again, and the traffickers in favor are back in business.

sentences.zh: 此風俗之壞，其漸二也。

translations.literal: This is the corruption of custom—the second gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second gradual decline: the corruption of public morals.

sentences.zh: 正德間，國柄下移，王靈不振，是以有安化、南昌之變，賴陛下起而整肅之。

translations.literal: During Zhengde, the handle of state shifted downward, and royal majesty was not invigorated—hence the disturbances at Anhua and Nanchang; fortunately Your Majesty arose and restored discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, authority slipped from the throne and imperial prestige waned, spawning the rebellions of the Prince of Anhua and the Prince of Ning—until Your Majesty restored order.

sentences.zh: 乃塞上戍卒近益驕恣。

translations.literal: Yet lately frontier garrison soldiers have grown increasingly arrogant and willful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately the garrison troops on the frontier have grown ever more insolent and unruly.

sentences.zh: 曩殺許巡撫而姑息，頃遂殺張巡撫而效尤。

translations.literal: Formerly they killed Governor Xu and were indulged; recently they killed Governor Zhang and others followed the example.
translations.idiomatic: When they murdered Governor Xu they were let off lightly; now they have murdered Governor Zhang, and others have taken it as precedent.

sentences.zh: 曩縛賈參將以立威，近又縛桂總兵而報怨。

translations.literal: Formerly they bound Deputy Commander Jia to establish authority; recently they bound Commander-in-chief Gui to settle scores.
translations.idiomatic: Once they seized Deputy Commander Jia to make an example; now they have seized Regional Commander Gui out of spite.

sentences.zh: 致榆關妖賊效之而戕主事，北邊庫吏仿之而賊縣官。

translations.literal: This caused demonic bandits at Yulin Pass to imitate them and slay a director; northern frontier warehouse clerks copied them and robbed county officials.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits at Yulin Pass followed suit and killed a director; warehouse clerks on the northern frontier copied them and murdered county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 陛下惑鄙儒姑息之談，牽俗吏權宜之計，遂使廟堂號令出於二三戍卒之口。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, deluded by vulgar Confucians' talk of indulgence and constrained by common officials' expedient schemes, has allowed court commands to issue from the mouths of two or three garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Misled by petty scholars preaching leniency and bound by clerks counseling compromise, Your Majesty has let the orders of state be dictated by a handful of mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 此國勢之衰，其漸三也。

translations.literal: This is the decline of national power—the third gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third gradual decline: the waning of national strength.

sentences.zh: 自逆瑾以來，以苞苴易將帥，故邊防盡壞，賴陛下起而申嚴之。

translations.literal: Since the rebel Jin, bribes have been exchanged for generals, so frontier defenses were utterly ruined—fortunately Your Majesty arose and reasserted strictness.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Jin's day, military commands have been bought with bribes and the frontier defenses ruined—until Your Majesty tightened discipline again.

sentences.zh: 然積弊已久，未能驟復。

translations.literal: Yet accumulated abuses have been long-standing, and swift recovery has not been possible.
translations.idiomatic: But the rot runs deep, and recovery cannot come overnight.

sentences.zh: 今朵顏蹢躅於遼海，羌戎跳梁於西川，北狄蹂躪於沙漠。

translations.literal: Now the Tümed prowl in the Liaodong seas, Qiang and Rong leap about in western Sichuan, and northern barbarians trample the desert sands.
translations.idiomatic: The Tümed linger off Liaodong, Qiang and Tibetans riot in western Sichuan, and northern tribes ravage the desert frontier.

sentences.zh: 寇勢方張，而食肉之徒不能早見預料，亟求制馭之方，乃假鎮靜之虛名，掩無能之實跡。

translations.literal: As bandit power is just expanding, meat-eaters cannot foresee early or anticipate, urgently seeking methods of control and restraint—instead they borrow the empty name of "pacification" to cover their actual tracks of incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: Enemies grow bolder by the day, yet the privileged officials at court cannot read the danger in time or devise a response—they merely invoke "pacification" to hide their own incompetence.

sentences.zh: 甚且詐飾捷功，濫邀賞賚，虛張勞伐，峻取官階，而塞上多事日甚。

translations.literal: Some even fraudulently ornament reports of swift victory, wantonly solicit rewards, falsely inflate punitive campaigns, and steeply seize official ranks—while frontier troubles grow daily worse.
translations.idiomatic: Some falsify victory reports, claim rewards they do not deserve, inflate their campaigns, and trade paper triumphs for rapid promotion—while the frontier burns hotter every day.

sentences.zh: 此外裔之強，其漸四也。

translations.literal: This is the strengthening of outer tribes—the fourth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fourth gradual decline: the growing strength of foreign enemies.

sentences.zh: 自逆瑾以來，盡天下之脂膏，輸入權貴之室，是以有劉、趙、藍、鄢之亂，賴陛下起而保護之。

translations.literal: Since the rebel Jin, all the realm's fat and grease have been poured into the chambers of the powerful—hence the disturbances of Liu, Zhao, Lan, and Yan; fortunately Your Majesty arose and protected the people.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Jin's day, the wealth of the empire has been drained into the coffers of the powerful, spawning the rebellions of Liu, Zhao, Lan, and Yan—until Your Majesty shielded the people.

sentences.zh: 乃近年以來，黃紙蠲放，白紙催征；

translations.literal: Yet in recent years, on yellow paper remissions are granted, on white paper collections are pressed;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in recent years the court issues edicts of tax relief on yellow paper, then sends white-paper orders to collect just the same;

sentences.zh: 額外之斂，下及雞豚；

translations.literal: Levies beyond the quota reach down even to chickens and pigs;
translations.idiomatic: Extra levies reach down to the farmer's last chicken and pig;

sentences.zh: 織造之需，自為商賈。

translations.literal: Requirements for weaving manufacture become trade for merchants themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Demands for imperial textile work have become a private business for eunuch traders.

sentences.zh: 江、淮母子相食，兗、豫盜賊橫行，川、陜、湖、貴疲於供餉。

translations.literal: On the Yangtze and Huai, mothers and children eat one another; in Yan and Yu, bandits roam at will; in Sichuan, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Guizhou, people are exhausted supplying rations.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yangtze and Huai people have been driven to cannibalism; in Yan and Yu bandits rule the roads; and Sichuan, Shaanxi, Huguang, and Guizhou groan under the burden of supplies.

sentences.zh: 田野嗷嗷，無樂生之心。

translations.literal: In the fields people wail in distress, with no heart to rejoice in life.
translations.idiomatic: Across the countryside people cry out in misery, with no will to go on living.

sentences.zh: 此邦本之搖，其漸五也。

translations.literal: This is the shaking of the state's foundation—the fifth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth gradual decline: the shaking of the nation's foundations.

sentences.zh: 正德朝，衣冠蒙禍，家國幾空，幸陛下起而收錄之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde court, the gentry suffered calamity, and state and family were nearly emptied—fortunately Your Majesty arose and gathered them back in.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, the gentry were struck down and the court all but emptied—until Your Majesty recalled the exiled and the sidelined.

sentences.zh: 乃未幾而狂瞽之言，一鳴輒斥。

translations.literal: Yet before long, wild and blind talk—one sound and immediate dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within a short time bold remonstrance is punished on first utterance.

sentences.zh: 昔猶謫遷外任，今或編配遐荒。

translations.literal: Formerly one might still be demoted to an outer appointment; now one may be registered and sent to remote wastes.
translations.idiomatic: Once dissenters were demoted to provincial posts; now they are banished to the frontier wilds.

sentences.zh: 昔猶禁錮終身，今至箠死殿陛。

translations.literal: Formerly one might still be confined for life; now one is beaten to death on the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were imprisoned for life; now they are beaten to death at the foot of the throne.

sentences.zh: 蓋自呂柟、鄒守益等去而殿閣空，顧清、汪俊等去而部寺空，張原、胡瓊等死而言路空。

translations.literal: Since Lü Nan, Zou Shouyi, and others departed, the Hall and Pavilion were emptied; since Gu Qing, Wang Jun, and others departed, the ministries and directorates were emptied; since Zhang Yuan, Hu Qiong, and others died, the avenue of speech was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: With the departure of Lü Nan and Zou Shouyi the inner court stands empty; with the departure of Gu Qing and Wang Jun the ministries stand empty; with the deaths of Zhang Yuan and Hu Qiong the channels of remonstrance stand empty.

sentences.zh: 間有一二忠直士，又為權奸排擠而違之，俾不通，致陛下耳囂目眩，忽不自知其在鮑魚之肆矣。

translations.literal: Occasionally one or two loyal and upright men exist, but they are squeezed out by powerful schemers and thwarted so they cannot get through—causing Your Majesty's ears to buzz and eyes to swim, suddenly not knowing yourself that you are in a fish market.
translations.idiomatic: The occasional honest voice is blocked by powerful schemers, until Your Majesty hears nothing but noise, sees nothing but glare, and no longer notices that you dwell in an atmosphere of corruption—as a man in a fish market grows deaf to the stench.

sentences.zh: 此人才之雕，其漸六也。

translations.literal: This is the withering of talent—the sixth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth gradual decline: the wasting away of talent.

sentences.zh: 正德朝，奸邪叠進，忠諫不聞，幸陛下起而開通之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde court, wicked men advanced in layers, loyal remonstrance was not heard—fortunately Your Majesty arose and opened the channels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, the wicked rose one upon another and loyal counsel went unheard—until Your Majesty reopened the path of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 顧閱時未久，而此風復見。

translations.literal: Yet the time of observation has not been long, and this trend has reappeared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet scarcely had the channels opened when the old pattern returned.

sentences.zh: 降心未懲其憤，逆耳或動諸顏。

translations.literal: One who humbles his heart is not yet spared the emperor's anger; words that grate the ear sometimes stir the royal countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Those who speak with humility are not spared the emperor's wrath; words that grate the ear still provoke the royal countenance.

sentences.zh: 不剿說而折人以言，即臆度而虞人以詐。

translations.literal: Without examining the statement, one refutes a person by his words; at once one surmises and suspects a person of deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Without weighing the argument, the emperor rejects the speaker; on mere suspicion he treats honest counsel as treachery.

sentences.zh: 朝進一封，暮投千里。

translations.literal: A memorial submitted in the morning; by evening one is cast a thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: Speak at dawn and by nightfall you are exiled a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 甚至三木囊頭，九泉含泣。

translations.literal: Some even suffer the three wooden cangues and sack over the head; in the nine springs they weep with grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Some are tortured with cangue and hood until they die with grievance unspoken.

sentences.zh: 此言路之塞，其漸七也。

translations.literal: This is the blockage of the avenue of speech—the seventh gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the seventh gradual decline: the sealing of the channels of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 正德朝，忠賢排斥，天下幾危，賴陛下起而主持之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde court, the loyal and worthy were cast out, and the realm was nearly endangered—fortunately Your Majesty arose and took charge.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, worthy men were driven out and the realm stood on the brink—until Your Majesty restored proper governance.

sentences.zh: 豈期一轉瞬間，憸邪投隙而起。

translations.literal: Who expected that in a single turning of the eye, sly wickedness would seize a gap and rise?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the blink of an eye, the cunning and corrupt have seized their opening.

sentences.zh: 飾六藝以文奸言，假《周官》而奪漢政。

translations.literal: They adorn the Six Arts to embellish wicked words, and borrow the Rites of Zhou to seize Han governance.
translations.idiomatic: They dress up treachery in the language of the Six Classics and invoke the Rites of Zhou to hijack imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 堅白異同，模棱兩可。

translations.literal: They argue hard-white sameness and difference, and equivocate both ways.
translations.idiomatic: They quibble over fine distinctions and speak from both sides of their mouths.

sentences.zh: 是蓋大奸似忠，大詐似信。

translations.literal: This is indeed great wickedness resembling loyalty, great deceit resembling faithfulness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the greatest treachery wears the mask of loyalty, and the deepest fraud the mask of sincerity.

sentences.zh: 王莽匿情於下士之日，安石垢面於入相之初。

translations.literal: Wang Mang hid his true designs in his days as a humble scholar; Wang Anshi smeared his face when first entering the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang concealed his ambitions while playing the humble scholar; Wang Anshi wore a mask of austerity when he first rose to power.

sentences.zh: 雖有聖哲，誰其辨之？

translations.literal: Even with a sage and wise ruler, who can discern them?
translations.idiomatic: Even a sage on the throne might fail to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 臣恐正不敵邪，群陰日盛。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that the upright cannot match the wicked, and the host of yin forces grows daily stronger.
translations.idiomatic: I fear righteousness cannot hold against corruption, and the dark faction grows stronger each day.

sentences.zh: 此邪正之淆，其漸八也。

translations.literal: This is the confusion of wicked and upright—the eighth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth gradual decline: the blurring of good and evil.

sentences.zh: 正德之世，大臣日疏，小人日親，致政事乖亂，賴陛下紹統，堂廉復親。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era, grand ministers were daily estranged, petty men daily intimate, causing administration to fall into disorder—fortunately Your Majesty succeeded to the line, and hall and inner curtain were again close.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, great ministers were pushed away and petty men drew close, until government broke down—until Your Majesty's accession restored intimacy between throne and court.

sentences.zh: 乃自大禮議起，凡偶失聖意者，譴謫之，鞭笞之，流竄之，必一網盡焉而後已。

translations.literal: Yet since the Great Rites controversy arose, all who by chance failed the imperial intent were rebuked and demoted, flogged, exiled and banished—always netting every one before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the Great Rites controversy began, anyone who once crossed the emperor has been demoted, flogged, or exiled—and not one has been spared.

sentences.zh: 由是小人窺伺，巧發奇中，以投主好，以弋功名。

translations.literal: Hence petty men watch and wait, cleverly launching strange hits to match the master's preferences and shoot for fame and office.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men seized the opportunity, tailoring flattery to the emperor's mood and trading sycophancy for rank.

sentences.zh: 陛下既用先入為主，順之無不合，逆之無不怒。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, having taken the first word as authority, finds nothing inconsistent in compliance and nothing but anger in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: Having set your mind on the first opinion offered, Your Majesty accepts whatever agrees with it and rages at whatever does not.

sentences.zh: 由是大臣顧望，小臣畏懼，上下乖戾，浸成睽孤，而泰交之風息矣。

translations.literal: Hence grand ministers look hesitantly, petty officials fear and dread; above and below are mutually alienated, gradually forming estrangement and isolation—and the wind of great harmony ceases.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers hesitate, junior officials tremble, the court falls out of step with the throne, estrangement deepens into isolation—and the spirit of open communion between ruler and subject is lost.

sentences.zh: 此君臣之睽，其漸九也。

translations.literal: This is the estrangement of ruler and minister—the ninth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the ninth gradual decline: the breach between emperor and court.

sentences.zh: 正德之世，天鳴地震，物怪人妖，曾無虛歲，賴陛下紹統，災異始除。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde era, heaven cried out and the earth quaked; strange things and human portents—never a year without them. Thanks to Your Majesty's inheriting the succession, calamities and anomalies were finally removed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhengde emperor, heaven thundered, the earth shook, and omens piled up year after year without respite. Only when Your Majesty took the throne did those portents begin to fade.

sentences.zh: 乃頃歲以來，雨雹殺禽獸，雷風拔樹屋，婦人產子兩頭，無極晝晦如夜，四方早潦，奏報不絕，曾何異正德之季乎？

translations.literal: Yet in recent years hail has killed birds and beasts, thunder-winds have uprooted trees and houses, women have borne two-headed children, at Wuji day turned dark as night, drought and flood have afflicted the four quarters, and memorial reports have never ceased—how is this any different from the end of the Zhengde reign?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in these last years hail has slaughtered livestock, storms have torn up trees and houses, women have given birth to two-headed infants, and at Wuji the daylight blackened like night. Drought and flood reports pour in from every province without pause. How is this unlike the closing years of Zhengde?

sentences.zh: 且京師陰霾之氣，上薄太陽，白晝冥冥，罕有暉采，尤為可畏。

translations.literal: Moreover the murky vapors of the capital press upward against the sun; by day all is dim and gloom, sunlight rarely breaks through—this is especially dreadful.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still, a murk hangs over the capital, blurring the sun so that even at noon the city stays dim and colorless—a sight that inspires real dread.

sentences.zh: 此災異之臻，其漸十也。

translations.literal: This is the arrival of calamities and portents—the tenth gradual trend.
translations.idiomatic: This is the tenth gradual decline: the return of calamities and portents.

sentences.zh: 此十者，天子有一，無以保四海。

translations.literal: Of these ten, if the Son of Heaven has even one, he cannot preserve the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor falls prey to even one of these ten trends, he cannot hold the realm together.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖明，何以致此？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sagely and clear-sighted—how could this have come about?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is wise and perceptive. How could things have reached this point?

sentences.zh: 無乃輔弼召之歟？

translations.literal: Might it not be that the chief ministers have summoned it?
translations.idiomatic: Surely your chief ministers have brought this upon the court?

sentences.zh: 竊見今日之為輔弼第一人者，徒以奸佞，伴食怙恩。

translations.literal: I have privately observed that today's foremost chief minister is nothing but treacherous and fawning, a companion at meals who relies on favor.
translations.idiomatic: I see that the man now ranked first among your ministers is nothing but a sycophant and schemer—a courtier who eats at the public table and trades on imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 致上激天變，下召民災，中失物望。

translations.literal: Above he provokes heavenly changes; below he summons popular calamity; in the middle he loses the people's regard.
translations.idiomatic: He provokes heaven's wrath above, brings disaster on the people below, and forfeits the respect of the court in between.

sentences.zh: 臣逆知其非天下之第一流，而陛下乃任信之，不至於魚爛不已。

translations.literal: Your servant anticipates in advance that he is not of the realm's foremost rank, yet Your Majesty nevertheless appoints and trusts him—not stopping until the fish rot through.
translations.idiomatic: I know in advance that he is no true leader of the realm, yet Your Majesty keeps trusting him—and the rot will not stop until the whole catch spoils.

sentences.zh: 願亟去其人，更求才兼文武如前大學士楊一清，老成厚重如今大學士石缶者，並置左右，庶弊政可除，天下可治。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would quickly remove this man and seek out others talented in both civil and military affairs, such as the former Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing, and steady, weighty men such as the present Grand Secretary Shi Fu, placing them together at your side—then perhaps corrupt government can be removed and the realm can be governed.
translations.idiomatic: Remove him at once, Your Majesty, and appoint men of real stature—soldier-statesmen like the former Grand Secretary Yang Yiqing and seasoned counselors like the present Grand Secretary Shi Fu. With such men at your side, corrupt rule might be cleared away and the empire set right.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞獻皇帝好賢下士，容物恕人，天下所共知也。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the Xian Emperor loved the worthy and honored scholars, was broad-minded toward things and forgiving toward people—this the whole realm knows in common.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard—and all the realm knows it—that the Xian Emperor loved talent, honored scholars, and was magnanimous and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 今議禮諸臣，一言未合，輒以悖逆加之。

translations.literal: Now the ministers who debated the rites, if one word did not accord, were immediately charged with treason and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Today, ministers who spoke on the rites controversy need only disagree once to be branded rebels.

sentences.zh: 謫配死徙，朝寧為空。

translations.literal: Demoted, banished, executed, and exiled—the court was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: They were demoted, banished, executed, and exiled until the court stood hollow.

sentences.zh: 此豈獻皇帝意？

translations.literal: Is this the Xian Emperor's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Can this be what the Xian Emperor would have wanted?

sentences.zh: 茍非其意，雖尊以天下，無當也。

translations.literal: If it is not his intent, though one is honored with the realm, it counts for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If this is not his will, then no honor in the world can make it right.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不起而用之，使駿奔清廟，以慰獻皇帝在天之靈哉！

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not rise and employ them, making them gallop to the clear temple, to comfort the Xian Emperor's spirit in heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Why not summon them back to service, Your Majesty, and send worthy men racing to the altars of state—thereby comforting the Xian Emperor's spirit in heaven?

sentences.zh: 疏反覆萬四千言，最為剴切，帝付之所司。

translations.literal: The memorial, developed at length to fourteen thousand words, was most incisive and earnest; the emperor handed it to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial ran to fourteen thousand words, repeated its points with cutting earnestness, and the emperor referred it to the appropriate ministry.

sentences.zh: 其所斥輔弼第一人，謂費宏也。

translations.literal: The foremost chief minister whom it denounced was Fei Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister it attacked as foremost among the counselors was Fei Hong.

sentences.zh: 珊律己清嚴，居官有威惠。

translations.literal: Shan disciplined himself with austere purity; in office he had both authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Shan held himself to a strict standard of integrity and governed with a balance of firmness and grace.

sentences.zh: 外艱歸，士民祠之名宦。

translations.literal: When he returned on account of a parent's death, gentry and commoners enshrined him among celebrated officials.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home to mourn a parent, local gentry and commoners erected a shrine to him as a distinguished official.

sentences.zh: 後副使胡東臯謁祠，獨顧珊嘆曰：「此吾師也。

translations.literal: Later Vice Commissioner Hu Donggao visited the shrine, turned alone toward Shan and sighed, saying: "This is my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Vice Commissioner Hu Donggao visited the shrine, he looked at Shan alone and sighed: "He was my teacher."

sentences.zh: 」服闋，以故官蒞廣東。

translations.literal: " When mourning ended, he took up his former post in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he resumed his former office and went to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 終四川按察使。

translations.literal: He ended as Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，有御史汪珊者，於嘉靖元年七月疏陳十漸。

translations.literal: Earlier there was Censor Wang Shan, who in the seventh month of the first year of Jiajing submitted a memorial setting forth ten gradual trends.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a censor named Wang Shan had submitted a memorial in the seventh month of Jiajing 1 describing ten gradual declines.

sentences.zh: 略言：「陛下初即位，天下忻然望治，邇來漸不如初。

translations.literal: It said in summary: "When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, the realm rejoiced and looked to good government; of late things have gradually fallen short of the beginning."
translations.idiomatic: It said in brief: "When Your Majesty first took the throne, the realm looked to you with hope; lately matters have steadily fallen short of that promise."

sentences.zh: 初每事獨斷，今戚裏左右，或潛移陰奪。

translations.literal: At first on every matter you decided alone; now consorts' kin and those at your side sometimes secretly shift decisions and seize them in the shadows.
translations.idiomatic: At first you decided every matter yourself; now imperial in-laws and court favorites quietly steer or steal your decisions.

sentences.zh: 初每事咨訪大臣，今禮貌雖隆，而實意日疏。

translations.literal: At first on every matter you consulted grand ministers; now though courtesy is lofty, real regard grows daily more distant.
translations.idiomatic: At first you consulted senior ministers on every issue; now the courtesies remain grand, but genuine trust grows thinner by the day.

sentences.zh: 初罷諸不經淫祠，今稍稍議復。

translations.literal: At first you abolished all improper licentious shrines; now there is gradual talk of restoring them.
translations.idiomatic: At first you shut down improper local cults; now people are already talking about bringing them back.

sentences.zh: 初屏絕玩好，今教坊諸司或以新聲巧伎進。

translations.literal: At first you barred frivolities and indulgences; now the Music Office and other agencies sometimes present new tunes and clever performances.
translations.idiomatic: At first you banished frivolous pleasures; now the Music Office and other agencies again offer fresh songs and clever entertainments.

sentences.zh: 初日覽奏章，今或置不省，輒令左右可否。

translations.literal: At first you reviewed memorials daily; now sometimes you set them aside unread and simply have those at your side approve or reject them.
translations.idiomatic: At first you read memorials every day; now some are left unread while attendants are told simply to approve or deny them.

sentences.zh: 初厘革冗食冗費，今騰驤勇士不行核實，禦馬實數不得稽察。

translations.literal: At first you reformed redundant stipends and wasteful spending; now soaring cavalry warriors are not verified, and the true count of imperial horses cannot be inspected.
translations.idiomatic: At first you cut redundant posts and wasteful spending; now cavalry rolls go unchecked and no one can audit the true number of imperial horses.

sentences.zh: 初裁革錦衣冒濫，今大臣近侍以迎立授世陰，舊邸旗校盡補親軍。

translations.literal: At first you trimmed the excess of the Embroidered Uniform Guard; now grand ministers and close attendants receive hereditary yin ranks for welcoming the enthronement, and the old residence's banner guards are all made up as personal troops.
translations.idiomatic: At first you reined in the Embroidered Uniform Guard's swollen ranks; now ministers and favorites receive hereditary honors for supporting your accession, and every banner guard from the old residence is enrolled as a personal soldier.

sentences.zh: 初中官有罪，懲以成法，今犯者多貸死，舉朝爭不得。

translations.literal: At first when eunuchs committed crimes they were punished by established law; now many offenders are spared death, and the whole court argues without success.
translations.idiomatic: At first eunuchs who broke the law were punished by statute; now most offenders are spared death, and the whole court protests in vain.

sentences.zh: 初中官有過不復任用，今鎮守守備營求易置，悻門復啟。

translations.literal: At first eunuchs with faults were not again employed; now garrison and defense eunuchs maneuver for reassignment, and the door of resentment opens again.
translations.idiomatic: At first disgraced eunuchs were never reappointed; now garrison and defense eunuchs lobby for new posts, and the old back doors are open again.

sentences.zh: 初納諫如流，今政事不便者，言官論奏，直曰『有旨』，訑訑拒人。

translations.literal: At first you received remonstrance like flowing water; now when policies are inconvenient, censorial officials submit memorials and are flatly told 'There is an edict,' sluggishly rejecting people.
translations.idiomatic: At first you welcomed remonstrance freely; now when censors protest bad policy they are brushed off with a flat 'The emperor has decided,' and turned away without a hearing.

sentences.zh: 」帝頗納其說。

translations.literal: " The emperor somewhat accepted his argument.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor largely accepted what he said.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出為河南副使，歷官至南京戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Vice Commissioner of Henan, and through successive offices reached Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was posted as Vice Commissioner of Henan and eventually rose to Right Vice Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 珊，字德聲，貴池人。

translations.literal: Shan, styled Desheng, was a native of Guichi.
translations.idiomatic: Shan, courtesy name Desheng, came from Guichi.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 6.

sentences.zh: 巡撫貴州時，討都勻叛苗有功。

translations.literal: When he was Grand Coordinator of Guizhou, he had merit in suppressing the rebellious Miao of Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Coordinator of Guizhou he earned distinction by suppressing the Miao rebellion at Duyun.

sentences.zh: 韋商臣，字希尹，長興人。

translations.literal: Wei Shangchen, styled Xiyin, was a native of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shangchen, courtesy name Xiyin, was from Changxing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in Jiajing 2.

sentences.zh: 授大理評事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Reviewing Official of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviewing official in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，商臣以「大禮」初定，廷臣下吏貶謫者無虛日，乃上疏曰：「臣所居官，以平獄為職。

translations.literal: The next winter, Shangchen, because the Great Rites had just been settled and court ministers were daily sent down to officials and demoted or banished, submitted a memorial saying: "The office I hold has as its duty the settling of cases."
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, with the Great Rites controversy freshly settled and court officials being punished or banished almost every day, Shangchen submitted a memorial: "My office exists to see justice done in the courts."

sentences.zh: 乃自授任以來，竊見群臣以議禮忤旨者，左遷則吏部侍郎何孟春一人，謫戍則學士豐熙等八人，杖斃則編修王思等十七人，以咈中使逮問，則副使劉秉鑒，布政馬卿，知府羅玉、查仲道等十人，以失儀就系，則御史葉奇、主事蔡乾等五人，以京朝官為所屬訐奏下獄，則少卿樂頀、御史任洛等四人。

translations.literal: Yet from the time I received appointment, I have privately seen that among the multitude of ministers who offended the throne by debating the rites: demoted—Vice Minister of Personnel He Mengchun, one man; banished to frontier service—Academician Feng Xi and others, eight men; beaten to death—Compiler Wang Si and others, seventeen men; arrested and interrogated for offending palace envoys—Vice Commissioner Liu Bingjian, Administration Commissioner Ma Qing, Prefects Luo Yu and Zha Zhongdao, and others, ten men; bound for breach of ceremony—Censor Ye Qi, Section Chief Cai Qian, and others, five men; imprisoned because capital officials were impeached by subordinates—Vice Minister of Ceremonies Yue Yi, Censor Ren Luo, and others, four men.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking office I have watched minister after minister punished for disputing the rites: He Mengchun, Vice Minister of Personnel, demoted; Feng Xi and seven other academicians banished to frontier service; Wang Si and sixteen other compilers beaten to death; Liu Bingjian, Ma Qing, Luo Yu, Zha Zhongdao, and six others arrested for offending palace envoys; Ye Qi, Cai Qian, and three others detained for breaches of ceremony; and Yue Yi, Ren Luo, and two others jailed because subordinates had impeached capital officials.

sentences.zh: 此皆不平之甚，上幹天象，下駭眾心。

translations.literal: These are all extreme in injustice; above they disturb heavenly signs, below they shock the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: These are grave injustices that offend heaven above and terrify the people below.

sentences.zh: 臣竊以為皆所當宥。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that all ought to be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: I believe every one of them deserves pardon.

sentences.zh: 況比者水旱疫癘，星隕地震，山崩泉湧，風雹蝗蝻之害，殆遍天下，有識莫不寒心。

translations.literal: Moreover of late there have been flood, drought, and pestilence; stars falling and earth quaking; mountains collapsing and springs gushing; harm from wind, hail, locusts, and nymphs—almost throughout the realm; the discerning are all chilled at heart.
translations.idiomatic: And now floods, drought, plague, falling stars, earthquakes, collapsing mountains, bursting springs, hail, locusts, and crop pests afflict nearly the whole realm. No thoughtful person can watch without dread.

sentences.zh: 及今平反庶獄，復戍者之官，錄死者之後，釋逮系者之囚，正告訐者之罪，亦弭災禳患之一道也。

translations.literal: If now one reverses wrongful cases in the various prisons, restores the offices of those banished to frontier service, records the descendants of the dead, releases those arrested and bound, and corrects the crimes of accusers who slander, this too is one path to quelling calamities and warding off disaster.
translations.idiomatic: To reverse unjust verdicts now, restore banished officials, provide for the families of the dead, free the imprisoned, and punish false accusers would itself be a way to calm heaven's anger and avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 」帝責以沽名賣直，謫清江丞，量移德安推官。

translations.literal: " The emperor rebuked him for fishing for reputation and selling integrity, demoted him to Assistant Magistrate of Qingjiang, and transferred him by measure to Push Officer of De'an.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accused him of courting fame under the guise of integrity, demoted him to assistant magistrate of Qingjiang, and later transferred him to judicial officer at De'an.

sentences.zh: 遷河南僉事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 討平永寧巨寇，以功受賞。

translations.literal: He suppressed and pacified the great bandits of Yongning and received reward for merit.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed the major bandit force at Yongning and was rewarded for his service.

sentences.zh: 伊王虐殺其妃，商臣論如律。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi cruelly killed his consort; Shangchen judged the case according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yi brutally murdered his consort, Shangchen prosecuted the case by the book.

sentences.zh: 嘗治裏居給事中杜桐殺人罪。

translations.literal: He once tried the case of Supervising Secretary Du Tong, living at home, for murder.
translations.idiomatic: He once tried Supervising Secretary Du Tong, then living in retirement, on a charge of murder.

sentences.zh: 桐構之吏部尚書汪鋐。

translations.literal: Tong framed him before Minister of Personnel Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Tong then framed Shangchen before Minister of Personnel Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 甫遷四川參議，遂以考察落職歸。

translations.literal: He had just been transferred to Administration Vice Commissioner of Sichuan when, on account of the performance review, he was dismissed from office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely been appointed Administration Vice Commissioner of Sichuan when a performance review stripped him of office and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 言官薛宗鎧、戚賢、戴銑輩交章救，不納。

translations.literal: Censorial officials Xue Zongkai, Qi Xian, Dai Xiao, and others submitted successive memorials to rescue him, but this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Xue Zongkai, Qi Xian, Dai Xiao, and others petitioned repeatedly on his behalf, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 家居數十年，卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home for several decades, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for decades before he died.

sentences.zh: 黎貫，字一卿，從化人。

translations.literal: Li Guan, styled Yiqing, was a native of Conghua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guan, courtesy name Yiqing, was from Conghua.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin Bachelor and appointed Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a bachelor and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 刷卷福建，劾鎮守內官尚春侵官帑狀，悉追還之。

translations.literal: Reviewing files in Fujian, he impeached the garrison eunuch Shangchun for encroaching on official coffers and fully recovered what had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: While auditing records in Fujian he impeached the garrison eunuch Shangchun for raiding public funds and recovered the full amount.

sentences.zh: 世宗入繼，貫請復起居註之制，命詞臣編類章奏備纂述，從之。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor entered the succession, Guan requested restoration of the Daily Record system and ordered literary officials to compile and classify memorials for compilation; this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Shizong Emperor succeeded to the throne, Guan urged restoration of the court diary and asked that literary officials compile memorials for the historical record; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 登極詔書禁四方貢獻，後鎮守中貴貢如故。

translations.literal: The enthronement edict forbade tribute from the four quarters; afterward the garrison eunuchs' tribute continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The accession edict banned local tribute from the provinces, yet garrison eunuchs kept sending gifts as before.

sentences.zh: 貫上言：「陛下明詔甫頒，而諸內臣曲說營私，希恩固寵。

translations.literal: Guan submitted a statement: "Your Majesty's clear edict has just been promulgated, yet the various inner officials twist arguments to seek private gain and hope for grace to secure favor."
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized: "Your Majesty's clear edict has only just been issued, yet palace eunuchs already twist the rules for private gain, trading flattery for favor."

sentences.zh: 其假朝命以征取者謂之額，而自挾以獻者謂之額外，罔虐百姓，致朝廷之澤壅而不流，非所以昭大信，彰君德也。」

translations.literal: What they levy under borrowed court authority is called the quota; what they bring on their own initiative is called beyond quota. They deceive and oppress the hundred surnames, causing the court's bounty to be blocked and not flow—this is not the way to display great trust and manifest the ruler's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: What they levy in the emperor's name they call the regular quota; what they seize on their own and present as gifts they call extra tribute. They cheat and abuse the people, choking off the court's bounty before it reaches them. That is no way to show the realm your sincerity or burnish imperial virtue."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，帝從玉田伯蔣輪請，於承天立興獻帝家廟，以輪子榮奉祀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, the emperor followed the request of Yutian Earl Jiang Lun and established a ancestral temple to the Xingxian Emperor at Chengtian, with Lun's son Rong conducting the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 2 the emperor granted Yutian Earl Jiang Lun's request to build a family temple to the Xingxian Emperor at Chengtian, with Lun's son Rong placed in charge of the rites.

sentences.zh: 貫言：「陛下信一諛臣之說，委祀事於外戚。

translations.literal: Guan said: "Your Majesty trusts the words of one fawning minister and entrusts sacrificial affairs to maternal kin."
translations.idiomatic: Guan protested: "Your Majesty has taken the word of a single sycophant and handed sacred rites over to a maternal relative."

sentences.zh: 神不歆非類，獻帝必將吐之。

translations.literal: Spirits do not accept offerings from improper persons; the Xian Emperor will surely reject them.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits do not accept offerings from the wrong hands—the Xian Emperor's spirit will surely reject them.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「國初，夏秋二稅，麥四百七十一萬，而今損九萬。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial saying: "At the founding of the dynasty, the summer and autumn two taxes in wheat were four million seven hundred ten thousand; now they have diminished by ninety thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he memorialized: "At the dynasty's founding the summer and autumn wheat levy stood at 4.71 million units; today it has fallen by ninety thousand."

sentences.zh: 米二千四百七十三萬，而今損二百五十萬。

translations.literal: In rice, twenty-four million seven hundred thirty thousand; now diminished by two million five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The rice levy was 24.73 million; it has now fallen by 2.5 million.

sentences.zh: 以歲入則日減，以歲出則日增。

translations.literal: By annual income, daily decrease; by annual expenditure, daily increase.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue shrinks year by year while spending grows.

sentences.zh: 乞敕所司通稽祖宗以來賦額及今日經費之數，列籍上聞。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty order the responsible offices thoroughly to audit the tax quotas since the ancestors and today's expenditure figures, list them in registers, and report upward.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the ministries to audit tax quotas since the founding of the dynasty and today's expenditures, set them out in registers, and report the figures to the throne.

sentences.zh: 知賦入有限，則費用不容不節。

translations.literal: Knowing that tax income is limited, expenditure cannot but be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Once the limits of revenue are known, spending cannot go unchecked.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 出按江西，父喪歸。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Jiangxi; on his father's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to inspect Jiangxi, then went home when his father died.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 會帝從張孚敬議，去孔子王號，改稱先師，並損籩豆佾舞之數。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor followed Zhang Fufu's proposal, removed Confucius's title of king, changed it to call him Former Teacher, and also reduced the numbers of ritual vessels, sacrificial dishes, and dance rows.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the emperor adopted Zhang Fufu's proposal to strip Confucius of his royal title, rename him Former Teacher, and cut back the ritual vessels, offerings, and dancers at his shrine.

sentences.zh: 編修徐階以諫謫。

translations.literal: Compiler Xu Jie was demoted for remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Xu Jie was banished for protesting the change.

sentences.zh: 禦制《改正祀典說》，頒示廷臣；

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed "An Explanation of Correcting the Sacrificial Canon" and circulated it among court ministers;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued his own essay, "On Reforming the Sacrificial Canon," and circulated it to the court;

sentences.zh: 而孚敬復為《祀典或問》，以希合帝意。

translations.literal: and Fufu again wrote "Questions and Answers on the Sacrificial Canon" to curry favor with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhang Fufu answered with his own "Questions on the Sacrificial Canon" to align himself with the emperor's views.

sentences.zh: 議已定，貫率同官合疏爭之。

translations.literal: When the decision was settled, Guan led his colleagues in a joint memorial to dispute it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the decision was fixed, Guan led his colleagues in a joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，曰：「貫等謂朕已尊皇考為皇帝，孔子豈反不可稱王？

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and said: "Guan and the others say that since I have already honored my imperial father as emperor, can Confucius on the contrary not be called king?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage: "Guan and his colleagues argue that because I have already elevated my father to emperor, Confucius somehow cannot remain a king?"

sentences.zh: 奸逆甚矣。

translations.literal: Treacherous and rebellious in the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: This is rank treason.

sentences.zh: 其悉下法司按治。

translations.literal: Let them all be sent down to the judicial offices for investigation and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hand them all over to the judicial authorities for prosecution.

sentences.zh: 」於是都御史汪鋐言：「比者言官論事，每挾眾以淩人曰：『此天下公議也』，不知倡之者止一人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Wang Gong said: "Of late when censorial officials discuss affairs, they each rely on the multitude to bully others, saying: 'This is the public opinion of the realm'—not knowing that the one who initiated it is only one person."
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-Chief Wang Gong then said: "Lately censors have banded together to intimidate the court, calling their views 'the opinion of the whole realm'—when in truth only one man started it."

sentences.zh: 請究倡議之人，明正其罪。

translations.literal: I request that the person who initiated the proposal be investigated and his crime clearly established.
translations.idiomatic: Investigate the ringleader and punish him openly.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而刑部尚書許贊等上其獄，當贖杖還職，帝特命褫貫為民。

translations.literal: Before long Minister of Justice Xu Zan and others reported on the case; the sentence should have been ransom and beating with return to office, but the emperor specially ordered that Guan be stripped and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Justice Xu Zan and others reported the verdict—commutation by fine and beating with restoration to office—the emperor personally ordered Guan stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家。

translations.literal: After a long time, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 方貫等上疏時，禮科都給事中華陽王汝梅亦率同官抗論，且曰：「陛下萬幾之余，留神典禮，甚盛舉也。

translations.literal: Just as Guan and the others were submitting their memorial, Wang Rumei of Huayang, Chief Drafter of the Ministry of Rites Section, also led his colleagues in resisting the proposal, saying: "Your Majesty, amid the myriad affairs, devotes attention to ritual and ceremony—a very grand undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: When Guan and his colleagues submitted their protest, Wang Rumei of Huayang, Chief Drafter of the Ministry of Rites Section, joined his colleagues in dissent, writing: "Your Majesty's attention to ritual amid the press of state affairs is a worthy undertaking."

sentences.zh: 但恐生事之臣望風紛起，今日獻一議，謂某制當革，明日進一說，謂某制當復，國家自此多事矣。

translations.literal: But I fear that troublemaking ministers, catching the wind, will rise in swarms: today offering one proposal that such-and-such an institution ought to be abolished, tomorrow advancing another view that such-and-such an institution ought to be restored—the state from this will have many troubles.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear opportunists will take this as a signal: today one faction proposes abolishing an old institution, tomorrow another urges restoring it. The court will never know peace.

sentences.zh: 況祖宗成法，守之百六十年，縱使少不如古，循而行之，亦未為過，何必紛紛事更易乎？

translations.literal: Moreover the ancestral established laws have been kept for one hundred sixty years; even if they fall somewhat short of antiquity, to follow and carry them out is still not excessive—why must there be clamor over changing and replacing things?
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of the founding emperors have stood for a hundred and sixty years. Even if they fall short of antiquity, following them would hardly be a crime. Why invite endless tinkering?

sentences.zh: 」帝覽奏，斥其違旨，以《祀典說》示之。

translations.literal: " The emperor read the memorial, rebuked him for violating the imperial intent, and showed him the "Explanation of the Sacrificial Canon."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor read the memorial, rebuked Wang for defying his will, and sent him the emperor's own "Explanation of the Sacrificial Canon."

sentences.zh: 汝梅，字濟元，由行人歷禮科都給事中。

translations.literal: Rumei, styled Jiyuan, rose from Courier to Chief Drafter of the Ministry of Rites Section.
translations.idiomatic: Rumei, courtesy name Jiyuan, rose from courier to Chief Drafter of the Ministry of Rites Section.

sentences.zh: 八年二月以災異求言。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eighth year, on account of calamities and portents, he sought statements.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year eight the emperor called for memorials in response to portents.

sentences.zh: 汝梅言：「比來章奏多逢迎，請分別忠佞，毋信諛言。

translations.literal: Rumei said: "Of late memorials mostly flatter and comply; I request distinguishing loyalty from treachery and not trusting sycophantic words."
translations.idiomatic: Rumei wrote: "Memorials lately are mostly flattery. Distinguish loyal counsel from sycophancy, Your Majesty, and do not trust adulation.

sentences.zh: 大臣奏事，近多留中，請悉付之公論。

translations.literal: When grand ministers submit affairs, of late many are kept within the palace; I request that all be entrusted to public discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Too many ministers' memorials are now held back unread. Submit them all to open debate."

sentences.zh: 人主之學，詞命非所重。

translations.literal: A ruler's learning—literary composition and edicts are not what should be emphasized.
translations.idiomatic: In a sovereign's education, polished prose and formal edicts ought not weigh heavily.

sentences.zh: 今一事之行，動煩宸翰，亦少褻矣。

translations.literal: Now for each matter's execution, frequently troubling the imperial brush—it is somewhat undignified.
translations.idiomatic: That every petty affair must await the emperor's own hand is undignified and exhausting.

sentences.zh: 宜仿祖宗故事，時禦平臺，召見宰執，面決大議，既省筆劄之勞，且絕壅蔽之害。

translations.literal: One ought to imitate the ancestral precedents, from time to time holding court at the platform, summoning the chief ministers, and deciding great affairs face to face—thus saving the labor of written memorials and cutting off the harm of obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the old imperial custom: hold open audiences on the terrace, summon the chief ministers, and decide weighty matters in person. That would spare endless paperwork and keep the court from going blind.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，忤旨。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and ran counter to the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, it displeased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及夏言請分祀天地，汝梅復偕同官力爭。

translations.literal: When Xia Yan requested separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, Rumei again joined his colleagues in forceful protest.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan proposed separate rites for Heaven and Earth, Rumei again led his colleagues in vehement opposition.

sentences.zh: 尋出為浙江參政，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Administrator of Zhejiang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted as Administrator of Zhejiang, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: 彭汝實，字子充，嘉定州人。

translations.literal: Peng Rushi, styled Zichong, was a native of Jiading Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Rushi, courtesy name Zichong, was from Jiading Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 正德十六年進士。

translations.literal: A presented scholar in the sixteenth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixteenth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Drafter of the Ministry of Personnel Section in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed drafter of the Ministry of Personnel section at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年疏言：「九江盜起，殺傷官軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he submitted a memorial saying: "Bandits arose at Jiujiang, killing and wounding officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing he memorialized the throne: "Bandits have risen at Jiujiang and killed government troops.

sentences.zh: 操江伍文定不即議剿，應城伯孫鉞擁兵不出，俱宜切責。

translations.literal: Wu Wending, Controller of the Yangtze, did not promptly discuss suppression; Sun Yue, Marquis of Yingcheng, held troops and did not march out—both ought to be sternly rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wending, river-defense commander, has not moved to suppress them; Sun Yue, Marquis of Yingcheng, holds his troops back. Both deserve stern rebuke.

sentences.zh: 」帝並從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved both points.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted both recommendations.

sentences.zh: 呂柟、鄒守益下獄，汝實抗章救。

translations.literal: When Lü Nan and Zou Shouyi were imprisoned, Rushi submitted a defiant memorial to save them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Nan and Zou Shouyi were thrown into prison, Rushi memorialized the throne in their defense.

sentences.zh: 又因災異上言：「邇者黃風黑霧，春早冬雷，地震泉竭，揚沙雨土。

translations.literal: Again, citing calamities and portents, he said: "Of late there have been yellow winds and black mists, early spring and winter thunder, earthquakes and springs running dry, sand blown up and earth raining from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Citing portents, he wrote again: "Yellow winds and black mists, thunder in winter and drought in spring, earthquakes, dried springs, sandstorms and rains of dust—

sentences.zh: 加以群小盛長，盜賊公行，萬民失業。

translations.literal: Added to this, petty men flourish, bandits walk openly, and ten thousand people lose their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: petty men thrive, bandits roam openly, and the people have lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 木異草妖，時時見告。

translations.literal: Trees with strange shapes and demonic plants are reported from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of freakish trees and uncanny plants arrive unceasingly.

sentences.zh: 天變於上，地變於下，人物變於中，而修省之詔無過具文。

translations.literal: Heaven changes above, earth changes below, human affairs change within—and yet the edicts calling for self-reform are nothing but empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven, earth, and men all show signs of disorder, yet the emperor's calls for self-reform remain hollow formulae.

sentences.zh: 廷陛之間，忠邪未辨，以逢迎為合禮，以守正為沽直。

translations.literal: Within the court and the steps of the throne, loyalty and treachery go undistinguished; flattery is taken as proper ritual conduct, and holding to integrity is treated as peddling blunt honesty.
translations.idiomatic: At court, loyalty and treachery go undistinguished. Flattery passes for propriety; steadfast integrity is mocked as self-righteousness.

sentences.zh: 長鯨巨鮞決綱自如，腴田甲第橫賜無已。

translations.literal: Great whales and giant sturgeons slip the net at will; fertile fields and grand mansions are lavishly bestowed without end.
translations.idiomatic: Great predators slip every net, while fertile estates and mansions are lavished without end.

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋已逾誌學，而經筵進講略無問難，黃閣票擬依常批答。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years have already passed the age of aspiration to learning, yet at the classics lectures there is almost no questioning and challenge; draft responses from the Yellow Pavilion are routinely approved.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is past fifteen, yet the lectures on the classics draw no probing questions, and drafts from the Grand Secretariat receive routine approval.

sentences.zh: 棄燕閑於女寵，委腹心於貂珰。

translations.literal: Leisure in the inner chambers is abandoned to female favorites; the innermost heart is entrusted to eunuchs in sable caps.
translations.idiomatic: Leisure is surrendered to palace women; the emperor's confidence is placed in eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 二廖諸張尚然緩死，李隆、蘇晉竟得無他。

translations.literal: The two Liaos and various Zhangs still received only delayed execution; Li Long and Su Jin escaped with no further penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The two Liaos and their Zhang allies received only delayed sentences; Li Long and Su Jin escaped entirely unscathed.

sentences.zh: 如此而望天意回，人心感，不可得矣。」

translations.literal: Hoping in this way for Heaven's intent to turn and people's hearts to be moved—it cannot be obtained."
translations.idiomatic: On such terms one cannot expect Heaven to relent or the people to be won over."

sentences.zh: 大學士費宏以子坐事被論不出，禮部侍郎溫仁和以慶王臺浤事聽勘。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Fei Hong, because his son was implicated in a case, was criticized and did not appear; Vice Minister of Rites Wen Renhe was under investigation for the Prince of Qing's Tai Yong affair.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fei Hong stayed away after his son's involvement drew censure; Vice Minister of Rites Wen Renhe faced investigation over matters involving the Prince of Qing's estate.

sentences.zh: 汝實言宜聽二臣避位，以明進退之義。

translations.literal: Rushi said the two ministers ought to be allowed to step aside to clarify the principle of advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi argued that both ministers should be permitted to withdraw, thereby honoring the code of when to serve and when to step down.

sentences.zh: 因薦石缶、羅欽順、顧清、蔣冕可代宏，李廷相、崔銑、湛若水、何瑭、許誥可代仁和。

translations.literal: He then recommended Shi Fou, Luo Qinshun, Gu Qing, and Jiang Mian to replace Hong, and Li Tingxiang, Cui Quan, Zhan Ruoshui, He Tang, and Xu Gao to replace Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Shi Fou, Luo Qinshun, Gu Qing, and Jiang Mian to succeed Hong, and Li Tingxiang, Cui Quan, Zhan Ruoshui, He Tang, and Xu Gao to succeed Renhe.

sentences.zh: 章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the appropriate department.

sentences.zh: 奸人王邦奇之訐楊廷和、彭澤也，汝實言：「邦奇先後兩疏，始為惶駭之語，終雜鄙褻之辭。

translations.literal: Regarding the villain Wang Bangqi's denunciation of Yang Tinghe and Peng Ze, Rushi said: "Bangqi's two memorials, one after another, began with language of alarm and ended mixed with vulgar and irreverent words.
translations.idiomatic: When the schemer Wang Bangqi denounced Yang Tinghe and Peng Ze, Rushi wrote: "Bangqi's two memorials began in tones of alarm and ended in vulgar, irreverent abuse.

sentences.zh: 中所引事，多顛倒淆惑，至謂費宏、石缶夜入楊一清門。

translations.literal: The affairs cited in them are mostly inverted and confused, going so far as to say Fei Hong and Shi Fou entered Yang Yiqing's gate by night.
translations.idiomatic: The incidents he cites are mostly garbled and contradictory, even alleging that Fei Hong and Shi Fou entered Yang Yiqing's house by night.

sentences.zh: 今不聞召問一清，一清又久不為白，何也？

translations.literal: Now we hear of no summons to question Yiqing, and Yiqing has long failed to clear himself—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yiqing has not been summoned to answer these charges, nor has he long since cleared his name. Why not?

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，廷和裁省冗員數萬，坐此叢怒罷去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession, Tinghe trimmed redundant posts by tens of thousands and for this was driven out amid collective wrath.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Your Majesty's reign, Tinghe cut tens of thousands of redundant posts and was driven from office by the fury of those he displaced.

sentences.zh: 今其長子業以狂愚發遣，亦可已矣。

translations.literal: Now his eldest son Ye has been banished for folly—that should suffice.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ye has already been banished for folly. Surely that is enough.

sentences.zh: 而群小蓄忿，蔓連不已，並其次子及婿又復下獄。

translations.literal: Yet petty men harbor resentment and extend the feud without end; even his second son and son-in-law have again been thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yet petty men nurse their grudges and widen the vendetta without end; even his second son and son-in-law have been thrown back into prison.

sentences.zh: 夫誣告之律，視其所誣輕重反坐，此國法也。

translations.literal: The law on false accusation: punishment is reversed according to the gravity of the charge falsely lodged—this is state law.
translations.idiomatic: The law on false accusation requires that the accuser suffer the penalty appropriate to the crime he invented. That is the law of the realm.

sentences.zh: 願追究主使之人，與告人同罪，毋令茍免，貽譏外蕃。

translations.literal: I pray that the masterminds be pursued and punished like the accusers, not allowed to escape, lest foreign domains mock us.
translations.idiomatic: Pursue the men behind the accusation and punish them as the accusers would be punished. Do not let them slip free and invite mockery from beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 汝實數言時政缺失，又嘗力爭「大禮」，為璁、萼等所惡。

translations.literal: Rushi repeatedly spoke on flaws in current policy and had also forcefully contested the "Great Rites," drawing hatred from Cong, E, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi repeatedly criticized failures of governance and had also fought the "Great Rites" controversy, earning the enmity of Zhang Cong, Gui E, and their faction.

sentences.zh: 以親老再疏請改近地教職，而舉貢士高任說、王表自代。

translations.literal: Citing aged parents, he twice memorialized asking to be transferred to a nearby teaching post, recommending presented scholars Gao Renshuo and Wang Biao to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Citing aged parents, he twice asked to be transferred to a teaching post nearer home, recommending the presented scholars Gao Renshuo and Wang Biao to take his place.

sentences.zh: 章下，吏部承璁、萼指，言：「汝實倡言鼓眾，撓亂大禮，且與御史方鳳、程啟充朋黨通賄。

translations.literal: When the memorial was sent down, the Ministry of Personnel, following Cong and E's lead, said: "Rushi incited the crowd, obstructed the Great Rites, and furthermore formed a faction with Censor Fang Feng and Cheng Qichong, taking bribes together.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was referred downward, the Ministry of Personnel, at Cong and E's direction, reported: "Rushi incited the crowd and obstructed the Great Rites. He also formed a faction with Censor Fang Feng and Cheng Qichong and exchanged bribes.

sentences.zh: 自知考察不容，乃欲辭尊居卑，不當聽其幸免。

translations.literal: Knowing he could not survive inspection, he now wishes to resign a lofty post for a humble one—it is not right to let him escape.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he cannot survive the next inspection, he now seeks to quit a high office for a low one. He must not be allowed to slip away.

sentences.zh: 」遂奪職閑住。

translations.literal: " His office was then stripped and he was ordered to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: " He was stripped of office and ordered to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 與啟充及徐文華、安磐皆同里，時稱「嘉定四諫」。
